info.title: KPOST Admin Module API
info.description:
REST API for the DKPOST **Admin Module** — the tenant (company) administration backend that manages organisation set-up, workplace/HR hierarchies, employee master data, role postings, product subscriptions and user onboarding.

### Persistence
All data is stored in **MongoDB** (database `admin_enterprise`) through Spring Data MongoDB repositories. Every domain object maps to a `table_*` collection; the Mongo `_id` (a 24-character hex `ObjectId`) is exposed as the `id` string property on every model.

### Uniform response envelope
Every endpoint in this module returns HTTP `200 OK` or `500 INTERNAL SERVER ERROR` carrying the same JSON envelope (see the `ApiResponseEnvelope` schema):

```json
{
  "value":      <payload — object, array or string>,
  "status":     "SUCCESS" | "FAILURE",
  "statusCode": 200 | 500,
  "urlPath":    "<endpoint path fragment>",
  "error":      "<exception message — only present on FAILURE>",
  "message":    "<human readable note — only on some endpoints>"
}
```

Note that this module does **not** emit `404 Not Found`; a missing MongoDB document is reported either as `200 OK` with `value: null` / `value: []`, or as `500` with `status: FAILURE`. Each operation below documents which of the two applies.

### Authentication
Protected endpoints expect a JWT in the `Authorization` header. The authentication filter decodes it and injects the `kpostID` and `companyID` request attributes that several endpoints read instead of taking them from the request body.

tags.name: Country & Address Reference Data
tags.description:
Global reference data used to populate country/dial-code pickers and to auto-fill address forms from a postal code.

Two different data sources sit behind this controller: the country catalogue lives in the `table_admin_country` MongoDB collection, while the two pincode lookups delegate to an **external KPOST address service** over HTTP — they do not read MongoDB at all, so their latency and failure modes are those of a remote call.

tags.name: Product Demo Requests
tags.description:
Pre-sales lead capture. Prospects who are not yet tenants submit a request for a product walkthrough; the KPOST sales team then works the queue.

Backed by the `table_admin_demo_request` MongoDB collection. Documents carry a `demo_status` field that defaults to `pending`. Because requesters are not yet customers, these two endpoints are the only ones in the module that are meaningfully **unauthenticated**.

tags.name: HR Set-Up Tier — Variables (Nodes)
tags.description:
The concrete **nodes** of a tenant's HR set-up hierarchy — the specific functions, teams and positions employees are attached to. Stored in the `table_admin_hr_setup_tier_variable` MongoDB collection and hung off the levels defined by **HR Set-Up Tier — Levels**.

As with the workplace tier, two independent link sets are stored side by side:

* `parent_variable_id` / `parent_attribute_id` — structural containment.
* `reporting_variable_id` / `reporting_attribute_id` / `reporting_json` — the reporting line, which may deliberately diverge from containment.

A node from this collection is what a role posting records in `last_hr_variable_id`, so deleting or re-parenting here has knock-on effects on employee placement.

tags.name: Departments
tags.description:
A tenant's departments — *Finance*, *Engineering*, *Operations* — the organisational unit that designations hang off.

Backed by the `table_admin_department` MongoDB collection, scoped by `companyId`. Unlike most entities in this module, `Department` declares **no** `@Field` mappings, so its properties persist under their camelCase Java names (`companyId`, `departmentName`) rather than snake_case — worth knowing when writing raw queries or Compass filters.

Every department carries a unique `abbreviation` and `code` generated by `abbreviationAndCodeCreation`; those codes are the building blocks of communication IDs (`userDetails/createCommunicationId`).

tags.name: Admin Details
tags.description: Profile of the **company administrator** — the single privileged person who owns a tenant's Admin Module set-up. Backed by the `table_admin_details` MongoDB collection, one document per company. The administrator record is what `rolePosting/getAssignedRolePostingEmployeeByCompanyId` returns alongside the employee list, so it must exist before role postings are surfaced in the UI.

tags.name: Designations
tags.description:
Job titles within a department — *Software Engineer*, *Finance Manager* — optionally nested via `parentDesignationId` to express a seniority chain.

Backed by the `table_admin_designation` MongoDB collection. Like `Department`, this entity declares no `@Field` mappings, so properties persist under their camelCase Java names.

A designation is scoped by **both** `companyId` and `departmentId`; its `abbreviation` and `code` (generated by `abbreviationAndCodeCreation`, which composes them against the parent department) are consumed by `userDetails/createCommunicationId`.

tags.name: Workplace Tier — Variables (Nodes)
tags.description:
The concrete **nodes** of a tenant's workplace hierarchy — *South Region*, *Chennai Zone*, *Adyar Branch* — each attached to a level defined by the **Workplace Tier — Attributes** controller.

Backed by the `table_admin_tier_variable` MongoDB collection. The tree is modelled with self-referencing string fields rather than embedded documents:

* `parent_variable_id` / `parent_attribute_id` — the structural parent, forming the tree.
* `reporting_variable_id` / `reporting_attribute_id` / `reporting_json` — a **separate** reporting line, which may differ from the structural parent (a branch can report to a regional office it does not structurally sit under).

Because there are no `$graphLookup` pipelines here, ancestor and descendant walks are performed with repeated round-trips in the service layer.

tags.name: Product Catalogue
tags.description:
The platform-wide catalogue of KPOST products a tenant can subscribe to, stored in the `table_product_master` MongoDB collection.

The catalogue itself is global, but the per-company read enriches each product with the calling tenant's subscription state: `isPurchased` and `productPurchase` are `@Transient` fields populated at read time by joining against `table_product_purchase` in the service layer — they are **never** stored on the product document.

tags.name: Project Catalogue
tags.description:
Global catalogue of KPOST projects/offerings — title, abbreviation and marketing copy. This is platform-level reference data shared by all tenants, not per-company project data.

Backed by the `table_admin_project_details` MongoDB collection. The abbreviations defined here are what prospects select in the demo-request form (`demo/createDemoRequest`).

tags.name: Employee Master Data
tags.description:
The employee record — personal details, addresses, employment data, education, work history and additional information — held as a single rich document per person.

Backed by the `table_admin_employee_details` MongoDB collection. This is the module's most heavily **embedded** document: `personalInformationObj`, `residentialObj`, `mailingObj`, `employmentObj`, `workExpObj` and `additionalObj` are nested sub-documents, `educationObj` is an array of them, and `workExpObj.experienceDetails` nests a further array — all stored inline rather than as references, so an employee is read and written in one round-trip. `locationName` is `@Transient` and never persisted.

An employee here is distinct from a **role posting** (`rolePosting`), which is what actually places the person in the workplace and HR hierarchies.

**Data-protection note** — these documents contain personal data including date of birth, mobile numbers, e-mail addresses, disability status and PAN card numbers. Every response below returns them unredacted.

tags.name: Workplace Hierarchy Links
tags.description:
The **edges** of the workplace graph: each document links one attribute/variable pair to its structural parent and, separately, to its reporting counterpart. Where `adminTierVariable` stores the nodes, this collection stores the wiring between them.

Backed by the `table_admin_workplace_hierarchy` MongoDB collection. Each document carries four id pairs — `attribute/variable`, `parent_attribute/parent_variable`, `reporting_attribute/reporting_variable` and `reporting_parent_attribute/reporting_parent_variable` — plus two denormalised **JSON string** snapshots, `workplace_json` and `reporting_json`, that capture the resolved path at write time. Those snapshots are copied onto role postings and are **not** refreshed when the hierarchy later changes.

The controller also exposes a small configuration read (`getOrganization`) that is not database-backed at all.

tags.name: HR Tier — Levels
tags.description:
Defines the **levels of a tenant's HR (people) hierarchy** — *Grade*, *Band*, *Cadre* and similar rungs — as opposed to the *workplace* hierarchy handled by the `adminTierAttribute` controller. The values sitting at each level are managed by **HR Tier — Variables** (`hrVariable`).

Backed by the `table_admin_hr_tier` MongoDB collection, scoped by `company_id`. Each level carries a generated `abbreviation` and `code` that feed into the `hr_json` string stamped onto role postings and employee records.

**Do not confuse this with `hrSetUpTierAttribute`**, which is a separate collection (`table_admin_hr_setup_tier_attribute`) with an identical shape — check which one your screen is wired to before writing.

tags.name: HR Tier — Variables (Nodes)
tags.description:
Values sitting at the levels defined by **HR Tier — Levels** (`hrTier`). Backed by the `table_admin_hr_variable` MongoDB collection.

The tree is built from `parent_variable_id` / `parent_attribute_id` string links, scoped by `company_id`. Documents here carry **no** `reporting_*` fields — this pair models HR structure only. If you need a reporting line, use the HR *set-up* tier (`hrSetUpTierVariable`) instead.

**Save is single-document here**, unlike every sibling controller in the module, whose `save` takes an array.

tags.name: Workplace Tier — Attributes (Levels)
tags.description:
Defines the **levels** of a tenant's workplace hierarchy: the named rungs such as *Region*, *Zone*, *Branch* or *Floor*. A level is an "attribute"; the concrete values sitting at each level are "variables", managed by the **Workplace Tier — Variables** controller.

Backed by the `table_admin_tier_attribute` MongoDB collection. Documents are scoped by `company_id`, so every tenant defines its own ladder of levels. Each attribute also carries a generated `abbreviation` and `code` used when composing employee workplace identifiers.

**Ordering caveat** — the collection stores no explicit rank field. The ladder's order is implied by the parent/child links on the variables, not by anything recorded here.

tags.name: HR Set-Up Tier — Levels
tags.description:
Levels of the **HR set-up** hierarchy, stored in the `table_admin_hr_setup_tier_attribute` MongoDB collection and paired with **HR Set-Up Tier — Variables** (`hrSetUpTierVariable`, collection `table_admin_hr_setup_tier_variable`).

This is the tier that role postings actually resolve against: a posting's `last_hr_tier_id` and `last_hr_variable_id` point into this pair, and the reporting chain returned by `hrSetUpTierVariable/getAllReportingHrTierVariableHierarchy` is what populates `reporting_hr_json`.

Structurally identical to `hrTier` (`table_admin_hr_tier`) but a **separate collection** — writing to one does not affect the other.

tags.name: Product ↔ Employee Licensing
tags.description:
Controls **which employees are licensed to use which purchased product**. Where `productPurchase` records that a company bought a product, this controller records who inside that company may actually open it.

Backed by the `table_product_employee_mapping` MongoDB collection. Each document links `employeeId`, `productId` and `companyId`, and carries the employee's `kpostId` — the cross-system identity used by downstream KPOST products.

**Cross-service integration point.** Two operations here are consumed by *other* KPOST services rather than by the Admin UI: `getKpostIDsByCompanyIdAndProductId` is called by KPOST to resolve company details from a product id, and `saveKpostIdForKams` is called by KAMS. `saveKpostIdForKams` is additionally the only endpoint in the module named explicitly in the security configuration's permit list, and the only one that writes **no audit entry** — treat changes to it as changes to a published contract.

tags.name: Holiday Calendar
tags.description:
A company's non-working days, optionally narrowed to a country and state so that regional offices can keep different calendars.

Backed by the `table_holiday` MongoDB collection — note the collection name breaks the `table_admin_*` convention used elsewhere in this module. Documents carry a `repeat_type` flag (`0` = current year, `1` = next year) and a `date` stored as an ISO local date.

**Authentication is mandatory for the read.** `getHoliday` takes the company from the `companyID` request attribute injected by the JWT authentication filter, not from a parameter — an unauthenticated call resolves the company to `null` and returns no holidays.

tags.name: Generic Variables (Base Hierarchy Nodes)
tags.description:
Values sitting at the levels defined by the **Generic Attributes** controller. Backed by the `table_admin_variable` MongoDB collection.

The tree is modelled with self-referencing `parent_variable_id` / `parent_attribute_id` string fields, scoped by `company_id`. Unlike the workplace and HR tier variables, documents here carry **no** `reporting_*` fields — this pair models structure only, with no separate reporting line.

tags.name: Users, Onboarding & Authentication
tags.description:
Everything about platform identity: company registration, sign-up, OTP mobile verification, login, password reset, and the per-company user directory.

Four MongoDB collections sit behind this controller:

| Collection | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `table_admin_user_details` | Per-company user directory with hierarchy scope |
| `table_admin_user_registration` | Company/organisation registration record |
| `table_admin_user_signup` | Login credentials (`user_id`, `password`) |
| `table_admin_otp_validation` | Issued OTPs with expiry and consumption flags |

**Public endpoints.** `sendOTP`, `validateOTP`, `signUp`, `login`, `registration`, `checkAvailability` and `generateUserIdSuggestions` are reachable without a token by design — they are the onboarding funnel. They are marked as such below and are the module's primary abuse surface: none of them is rate-limited in this codebase.

**Password handling.** `UserSignUp.password` is a plain field on the document and the security configuration wires a `NoOpPasswordEncoder`. Treat every credential-carrying request and response here as sensitive, and do not log them.

tags.name: Product Subscriptions
tags.description:
A tenant's subscriptions to catalogue products — what was bought, on which plan, and until when.

Backed by the `table_product_purchase` MongoDB collection. Each document links a `product_id` to a `company_id` with a `subscription_type`, a `subscription_date` defaulted to the moment of creation, and an `end_date`. These records are what `productMaster/productList/{companyId}` joins against to decide a product's `isPurchased` flag.

**Entitlement note** — nothing in this module enforces `end_date`; an expired subscription still resolves as purchased unless the caller filters on the date itself.

tags.name: Generic Attributes (Base Hierarchy Levels)
tags.description:
The base, un-tiered attribute catalogue: named hierarchy levels held in the `table_admin_attribute` MongoDB collection and paired with the **Generic Variables** controller (`table_admin_variable`).

This is the simplest of the four level/value pairs in the module — unlike `adminTierAttribute` and `hrSetUpTierAttribute` its documents carry no `abbreviation` or `code`, only `company_id` and `attribute_name`. Confirm with the platform team which pair a new screen should target before wiring against this one; the tier-specific controllers are what the workplace and HR hierarchy builders use.

tags.name: Employee ↔ Role Posting Mapping
tags.description:
The join record binding an employee to a role posting, stored in the `table_admin_role_employee_mapping` MongoDB collection.

Each document is a three-way link — `company_id`, `employee_id`, `role_posting_id` — stamped with a `created_date` defaulted to the current date by the entity. Because a new document is written per assignment rather than an existing one being updated, the collection doubles as an **append-only assignment history**.

Only a write endpoint is exposed here; the corresponding reads live on the `rolePosting` controller.

tags.name: Workplace Locations
tags.description:
Physical sites — offices, plants, branches — pinned to a node of the workplace hierarchy. A location is where a role posting is physically anchored via `workplace_location_id`.

Backed by the `table_admin_location` MongoDB collection. This entity declares **no** `@Field` mappings, so all properties persist under their camelCase Java names (`attributeId`, `workPlaceLocation`, `reportingWorkplaceLocationId`, …).

Two links coexist on each document, mirroring the workplace tier: `attributeId` /`variableId` place the site in the hierarchy, while `reportingWorkplaceLocationId` names the site it reports to — which need not be its structural parent.

**Note** — despite the address fields (`pincode`, `state`, `city`, `area`), no geospatial index or `$near` query is involved anywhere in this controller; all lookups are plain equality matches.

tags.name: Role Postings
tags.description:
The heart of the Admin Module. A **role posting** is a seat in the organisation: a position defined by a workplace node, an HR node and a physical location, which an employee may or may not currently occupy. Creating the seat and filling it are separate steps — a posting with a null `employee_id` is a vacancy.

Backed by the `table_admin_role_posting` MongoDB collection. Key modelling points:

* **Denormalised path snapshots.** `workplace_json`, `hr_json`, `reporting_workplace_json` and `reporting_hr_json` are JSON **strings** capturing the resolved hierarchy path at the moment the posting was written. They are not refreshed when the hierarchy later changes, which is deliberate — a posting records where the person sat *then*.
* **Cross-system identity.** `kpost_id`, `ksmacc_id`, `ksmacc_company_id` and `ksmacc_display_name` tie the seat to the KSMACC and KPOST platforms; several operations here make **outbound calls** to those services in addition to writing MongoDB.
* **Lifecycle via `active_status`.** Suspension and termination flip this boolean and record `reason`, `remarks`, `duration` and `rejoining_date` rather than deleting anything. A scheduler reactivates postings whose `rejoining_date` has arrived.
* **Transient enrichment.** `employeeDetails`, `locationName`, `companyName`, `isPromoted`, `isTransfered`, `isMapped` and friends are `@Transient` — computed on read, never stored.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — re-wires an edge: changes a position's structural parent or its reporting target, or refreshes the denormalised JSON snapshots.

**Database behaviour** — replaces the document identified by `id` in `table_admin_workplace_hierarchy`. Whole-document write: fields omitted from the body are persisted as `null`, which would silently unwire the position — send the complete link.

**Side effects** — updating `workplaceJson` / `reportingJson` here does **not** propagate to role postings already created; those hold their own copy taken at posting time. Audited as `workplaceHierarchy/update`.

requestBody.description: Complete hierarchy link document including the `id` to update. Omitted fields are written as `null`.

200.description: `value` is the updated hierarchy link document.

500.description: No document matched the supplied `id` (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — records one edge of the workplace graph after the nodes themselves have been created, wiring a position to its structural parent and its reporting counterpart.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces a single document in `table_admin_workplace_hierarchy`. Omit `id` to insert with a generated `ObjectId`; supply an existing `id` to replace that document in full. Takes **one object, not an array**, unlike the tier controllers' bulk `save`.

**Side effects** — `workplaceJson` and `reportingJson` are stored as opaque strings and become the snapshot that role postings copy. Because nothing re-derives them later, a stale snapshot here propagates silently into every posting created afterwards. Audited as `workplaceHierarchy/save`.

requestBody.description: A single hierarchy link. `attributeId`/`variableId` identify the position being wired; the `parent*` pair gives its structural parent and the `reporting*` pair its reporting target. `workplaceJson` and `reportingJson` are **serialised JSON strings**, not nested objects — escape them accordingly.

500.description: The service returned nothing (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

200.description: `value` is the persisted hierarchy link document with its generated `id`.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or a JSON array was sent where a single object is expected.

post.summary: Query workplace hierarchy links by example
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the flexible read behind the hierarchy graph view: pass whichever id fields you know and get back the matching edges.

**Database behaviour** — the service builds the filter from the **non-null** fields of the submitted entity and queries `table_admin_workplace_hierarchy`. Which combinations are supported is decided in `WorkPlaceHierarchyServiceImpl`, so consult it before relying on an unusual field mix.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`workplaceHierarchy/getWorkPlaceHierarchy`).

requestBody.description: Probe object. Populate only the id fields you want to filter on — typically `parentAttributeId` + `parentVariableId` to fetch a node's children, or `attributeId` + `variableId` to fetch one position's wiring. Leave the rest null.

200.description: `value` is the array of matching hierarchy link documents; `[]` when the filter matches nothing.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes an edge from the workplace graph, detaching a position from its parent and reporting target.

**Database behaviour** — a hard delete against `table_admin_workplace_hierarchy`. The document is physically removed; there is no soft-delete flag.

**Side effects** — destructive. The nodes themselves survive in `table_admin_tier_variable`; only the wiring is lost, so the position drops out of the graph view while remaining selectable elsewhere. Audited as `workplaceHierarchy/delete`.

**Response note** — the success envelope carries no `value` key; branch on `status`.

requestBody.description: The hierarchy link to delete, identified by its `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`).

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the delete threw.

200.description: Link deleted. Envelope carries `status: SUCCESS` and `statusCode: 200` but no `value`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — renames a value or re-parents it within the generic hierarchy.

**Database behaviour** — replaces the document identified by `id` in `table_admin_variable`. Whole-document write: any field omitted from the body is persisted as `null`.

**Side effects** — changing `parentVariableId` moves the node's entire subtree implicitly, since children are resolved by parent id rather than by an embedded path. Audited as `variable/update`.

requestBody.description: Complete variable document including the `id` to update. Omitted fields are written as `null`.

500.description: No document matched the supplied `id` (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

200.description: `value` is the updated variable document.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — saves a whole sibling group of hierarchy values in one call.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces documents in `table_admin_variable`, one per array element. Elements without an `id` are inserted with a generated `ObjectId`; elements carrying an `id` replace that document in full. The service derives `abbreviation` and `code` from `variable_name`.

**Side effects** — nothing validates that `attributeId` or `parentVariableId` reference existing documents, so a wrong id silently creates an unreachable node. Audited as `variable/save`.

requestBody.description: Array of variables. Per element supply `companyId`, `attributeId` (the level this value belongs to) and `variableName`. Leave `parentVariableId` and `parentAttributeId` null for root values.

200.description: `value` is the array of persisted variables with `id`, `abbreviation` and `code` populated.

500.description: The service returned an empty list (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the bulk write threw. Partial writes are not rolled back.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a field has the wrong type.

post.summary: List the direct children of a variable
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — lazy expansion of the generic hierarchy tree: fetch one node's immediate children as the user drills down.

**Database behaviour** — a two-field derived query `find({ "parent_variable_id": <parentVariableId>, "company_id": <companyId> })` over `table_admin_variable`. Only direct children are returned — each additional depth level costs another call.

**Root nodes** — pass `parentVariableId` as `null` to list the top of the tree.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`variable/getVariable`).

requestBody.description: Only `parentVariableId` (24-character hex `ObjectId`, or `null` for roots) and `companyId` are read.

200.description: `value` is the array of direct child variables; `[]` for a leaf node or an unknown parent.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes a value from the generic hierarchy.

**Database behaviour** — a hard delete against `table_admin_variable`. The document is physically removed; there is no soft-delete flag.

**Side effects** — destructive and not cascading. Child variables keep pointing at the deleted `parent_variable_id` and drop out of the tree walk. Delete leaves first, or re-parent the children. Audited as `variable/delete`.

**Response note** — the success envelope carries no `value` key; branch on `status`.

requestBody.description: The variable to delete, identified by its `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`).

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the delete threw.

200.description: Variable deleted. Envelope carries `status: SUCCESS` and `statusCode: 200` but no `value`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — step two of mobile verification: confirms the code the user received by SMS.

**Public** — no authentication required.

**Database behaviour** — looks up the most recent matching document in `table_admin_otp_validation` for the mobile number, compares the submitted `otp`, and checks `expire_date` against now. On success it flips `otp_validation_status` to `'Y'` so the code cannot be replayed; expired codes are marked through `otp_expire_status`.

**Side effects** — consumes the OTP. A second call with the same code fails.

**Abuse surface** — no attempt counter and no lockout is implemented here, so an unauthenticated caller can brute-force a short numeric OTP within its 10-minute window. Add attempt limiting before exposing this publicly.

**Failure reporting** — on the negative path the service's own explanation (wrong code, expired, already used) is placed in `message`, which is what you should show the user.

requestBody.description: `mobileNumber` and `otp` are the essentials, matching the pair issued by `sendOTP`; `dialCode` is a **number**. `type` should mirror the `requestType` used when the OTP was sent. Do not send the status flags or dates — they are managed server-side.

200.description: OTP accepted and consumed. `status` is `SUCCESS` and `message` reads *OTP has been validated successfully.*

400.description: Malformed JSON, or `dialCode` sent as a string rather than a number.

500.description: Validation failed — wrong code, expired code, or a code already consumed. `status` is `FAILURE` and `message` carries the service's explanation. An exception instead populates `error`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — amends a user's profile or re-scopes their hierarchy access by changing `variableIds` / `reportingVariableIds`.

**Database behaviour** — updates the document identified by `id` in `table_admin_user_details`. The `variableIds` arrays are **replaced wholesale**, not merged — send the complete list you want the user to end up with, or you will silently revoke access to the nodes you left out.

**Side effects** — changes what the user can see in the admin UI on their next request. Credentials in `table_admin_user_signup` are untouched. Audited as `userDetails/update`.

**Naming note** — the Java method is called `updateDepartment`, a copy-paste leftover. It updates a user, not a department.

requestBody.description: Complete user document including the `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`) to update. Include the full `variableIds` list you want retained.

200.description: `value` is the updated `UserDetailsEntity`.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or `companyId` sent as a string rather than a number.

500.description: No document matched the supplied `id` (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — completes self-service onboarding by creating the credentials the user will log in with. Call it after the mobile number has been verified through `sendOTP` / `validateOTP` and after `checkAvailability` has confirmed the chosen `userID` is free.

**Public** — no authentication required.

**Database behaviour** — inserts a document into `table_admin_user_signup` with `created_date` defaulted to now.

**Credential warning** — `password` is transmitted and **stored in clear text**; the security configuration wires a `NoOpPasswordEncoder`. Use TLS and keep this payload out of logs. Introducing a real encoder is the single highest-value hardening change available in this module.

**Race condition** — `checkAvailability` does not reserve the `userID`, so two concurrent sign-ups can both pass the check. Be prepared for a `500` on a duplicate.

**Side effects** — creates a usable login. Audited as `userDetails/signUp`.

requestBody.description: New account details. `userID` is the login name and must be unique; `password` is clear text over the wire. `requestType` is `@Transient` and used only for flow control — it is never persisted. Omit `id` and `createdDate`.

500.description: The service returned nothing (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key) — commonly a `userID` taken between the availability check and this call — or the write threw.

200.description: `value` is a `SignUpResponse` carrying the new account's `id`, `country`, `name`, `mobileNumber`, `emailID` and `userID`. The password is not echoed.

post.summary: Send a one-time password by SMS (public)
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — step one of mobile verification during sign-up and password reset. Issues an OTP and texts it to the supplied number.

**Public** — no authentication required.

**Database behaviour** — inserts a document into `table_admin_otp_validation` carrying the generated `otp`, the `send_date`, a computed `expire_date`, and the `otp_validation_status` / `otp_expire_status` flags (both `'N'` initially). `created_by` defaults to `USER`.

**Side effects — sends a real SMS.** The service dispatches the message through the KPOST SMS gateway, which costs money and reaches an actual handset. The OTP is valid for **10 minutes**.

**Abuse surface** — there is no rate limiting, no captcha and no per-number throttle in this codebase. An unauthenticated caller can trigger unlimited SMS to an arbitrary number. Put a rate limit in front of this route before exposing it publicly.

**`requestType`** — selects the SMS template and the purpose of the OTP (for example sign-up versus password reset); see `KpostSMSTemplate`.

requestBody.description: `mobileNumber` is the national number without the dial code; `dialCode` is a **number** (91 for India). `requestType` selects the SMS template and OTP purpose. `userID` is optional context.

200.description: OTP dispatched. `status` is `SUCCESS` and `message` reads *OTP has been sent to the given mobile number. Valid for 10 minutes only*. The OTP itself is **not** returned.

500.description:
Two cases:

* **Gateway or validation failure** — `message: "unable to send OTP"`, `status: FAILURE`, no `error` key.
* **Exception** — `error` carries the message.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or `dialCode` sent as a string rather than a number.

post.summary: Create a user in the company directory
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — adds a user to a company's directory and scopes them to parts of the workplace/HR hierarchy, controlling what they can see in the admin UI.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces a document in `table_admin_user_details`. Omit `id` to insert with a generated `ObjectId`. Note `variableIds` and `reportingVariableIds` are stored as **arrays of free-form maps** (`List<Map<String, Object>>`), so their inner shape is not schema-enforced and varies by caller.

**Type gotcha** — `companyId` on this entity is an **`int`**, unlike the `String` `companyId` used by almost every other collection in the module. Sending a quoted string here produces a `400`.

**Side effects** — creates a directory entry, distinct from the login credentials held in `table_admin_user_signup`. Audited as `userDetails/save`.

requestBody.description: The user to create. `companyId` is a **numeric** tenant id. `variableIds` scopes the user to hierarchy nodes and `reportingVariableIds` to their reporting branches; both are arrays of loose maps.

500.description: The service returned nothing (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or `companyId` sent as a string rather than a number.

200.description: `value` is the persisted `UserDetailsEntity` including its generated `id`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — completes the forgotten-password flow after the user's mobile number has been verified through `sendOTP` / `validateOTP`.

**Public** — no authentication required.

**Database behaviour** — updates the `password` field of the matching `table_admin_user_signup` document. Because a `NoOpPasswordEncoder` is configured, the new password is stored in clear text.

**Authorisation gap — treat as a finding.** This endpoint takes only a `userID` and a new `password`. Nothing in the controller ties the request back to a validated OTP, an existing session, or the old password, so whether a caller may reset a given account rests entirely on whatever check `UserServiceImpl.resetPassword` performs. Review that method before exposing this route publicly; if the check is not there, any unauthenticated caller who knows a `userID` can take over the account.

**Side effects** — changes credentials. Audited as `userDetails/resetPassword` with the submitted `userID` as the actor.

requestBody.description: `userID` identifies the account and `password` is the new clear-text credential. Send over TLS only and never log this payload.

200.description: Password changed. `value` reads `Password Changed SuccessFully!!!`.

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — an unknown `userID`, or a rejected pre-condition — reported as `error: "Password not updated!!.Please try later."`. An exception instead puts its own message in `error`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — tenant onboarding. Captures the organisation's identity, address, licence counts and the primary contact, creating the company record everything else in the module hangs off.

**Public** — no authentication required; this is the first call a new customer makes.

**Database behaviour** — inserts a document into `table_admin_user_registration`. `typeOfOrganization` should be one of the values returned by `workplaceHierarchy/getOrganization`, and address fields can be pre-filled from `country/getAddressUsingPincode`.

**Credential warning** — this request carries a `password` in clear text, and the saved document stores it as-is (the security configuration uses a `NoOpPasswordEncoder`). Send it over TLS only and keep it out of logs and analytics.

**Side effects** — creates the tenant. Audited as `userDetails/registration`, using the submitted `userID` as the actor since no authenticated principal exists yet.

requestBody.description: Organisation registration. `noOfEmployee` and `noOfUserLicenses` are **integers**. `logo` is typically a URL or base64 data URI. Nothing is validated server-side, so enforce required fields in the client.

500.description: The service returned nothing (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw — for example a duplicate `user_id`.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or `noOfEmployee` / `noOfUserLicenses` sent as strings rather than numbers.

200.description: `value` is the persisted `UserRegistration` document — **including the `password` field**, so do not surface it in a UI.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the login call. Verifies credentials against the sign-up collection and returns the caller's identity.

**Public** — no authentication required; this is where a session begins.

**Database behaviour** — looks up the `user_id` in `table_admin_user_signup` and compares the supplied `password`. Because a `NoOpPasswordEncoder` is configured, the comparison is against the clear-text stored value.

**Where is the token?** The response carries a `SignUpResponse` — identity fields only. Confirm with `UserServiceImpl.login` how the JWT that the authentication filter expects in `Authorization: Bearer <token>` is actually delivered; it is not part of the `SignUpResponse` shape.

**Abuse surface** — no rate limiting, no attempt counter and no lockout. Combined with clear-text password storage, this route deserves a throttle in front of it.

**Side effects** — none in MongoDB beyond the audit entry (`userDetails/login`), which records the submitted `userID` whether or not the login succeeded.

requestBody.description: Only `userID` and `password` are required. Send over TLS; never log this payload.

200.description: Credentials accepted. `value` is a `SignUpResponse` with the user's identity fields.

500.description: Authentication failed — `status: FAILURE` with `error: "Enter valid user name and password"`. Note this is a *credential* rejection reported as a server error rather than a `401`; branch on the `error` text or on `status`.

example.error: Enter valid user name and password

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — when the sign-up form reports a chosen `userID` as taken, this offers alternatives derived from the user's name and mobile number so they do not have to guess.

**Public** — no authentication required.

**Database behaviour** — generates candidate identifiers from `userName` and `mobileNumber`, then filters them against `table_admin_user_signup` so only free ones are returned. Read-only.

**Not a reservation** — suggestions are not held. A candidate can be claimed by someone else before the user submits, so `signUp` may still fail.

**Privacy note** — the suggestions are derived from the submitted name and mobile number, so they may embed fragments of both.

requestBody.description: Only `mobileNumber` and `userName` are read — both are the raw material for the generated candidates.

200.description: `value` is an array of available user ID strings.

500.description: No free candidate could be generated — typically a blank `userName` or `mobileNumber` (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key) — or a read threw.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — composes the KPOST **communication identifier** for a person from their department, designation and role — the human-readable handle used to address them across KPOST products.

**Database behaviour** — reads the abbreviation/code values previously generated for the department and designation (see `department/abbreviationAndCodeCreation` and `designation/abbreviationAndCodeCreation`) and assembles them into an identifier, checking existing records for collisions. Whether the result is persisted or merely computed is decided in `UserServiceImpl.createCommunicationId` — verify before assuming the id is reserved.

**Audit quirk** — unlike its neighbours this method does not receive the `HttpServletRequest`, so it audits using the `designation` string as the actor. Audit rows for this route therefore carry a designation name where a user identifier normally appears.

**Side effects** — see the persistence note above; audited as `userDetails/createCommunicationId`.

requestBody.description: The three components of the identifier. Values are matched against existing department and designation records, so supply the names exactly as stored.

200.description: `value` is the generated communication ID string.

500.description: The generator returned an empty value — typically an unknown department or designation, or a blank `role` — or a read threw.

post.summary: Check whether an identifier is free (public)
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — live validation on the sign-up form: tells the user whether the `userID`, mobile number or e-mail they typed is already taken.

**Public** — no authentication required.

**Database behaviour** — an existence check against `table_admin_user_signup`. `requestType` selects which field is checked — see `UserServiceImpl.checkAvailability` for the accepted values, which correspond to the `mobile`, `emailID` and `userID` constants in `KPOSTConstants`.

**Not a reservation** — availability is a point-in-time answer. Nothing is locked, so two concurrent sign-ups can both be told the same `userID` is free and one will fail at `signUp`.

**Inverted status semantics — read carefully.** "Available" is the `200` case and "already taken" is the `500` case. A `500` here is the *normal* answer for a name that is in use, not a fault. `error` reads *Already Available!! Try something*, which despite its wording means the identifier is **not** available.

**Enumeration risk** — this endpoint lets an unauthenticated caller confirm whether a given mobile number or e-mail is registered. Rate-limit it.

requestBody.description: `requestType` selects which identifier to check (`userID`, `mobile` or `emailID`); populate the corresponding field with the value to test. The audit entry always records `mobileNumber` as the actor, regardless of which field is being checked.

500.description: Usually **not an error**: the identifier is already taken, reported as `status: FAILURE` with `error: "Already Available!! Try something"`. A genuine read failure instead puts the exception text in `error`.

200.description: The identifier is **free**. `value` reads `<requestType> Is Available!!`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the workhorse for changing a seat: assigning an employee to a vacancy, moving someone to a new location or HR position (transfer), or promoting them.

**Database behaviour** — updates the document identified by `id` in `table_admin_role_posting`, recomputing the `*_json` path snapshots for the new anchors.

**Side effects — reaches beyond MongoDB.** Depending on the transient flags on the body, the service may also issue outbound calls to the KSMACC/KPOST services and write supporting records:

* `isPromoted` / `isTransfered` — record the change on the employee's `promotionDetails` / `transferDetails`.
* `isKpostIDRequired` — generate and stamp a new KPOST identifier.
* `isMapped` — maintain the product/employee mapping alongside the posting.

The operation is **not transactional** across those steps: a failure after the MongoDB write leaves the posting updated but the integration incomplete.

**Error-reporting gap** — on the exception path this method deliberately does **not** populate the `error` key (the line is commented out in the source), so a `500` here carries `status: FAILURE` and nothing else. Diagnose from the server-side stack trace, not the response body.

Audited as `rolePosting/update`.

requestBody.description: The posting to update, identified by `id`. Set the transient flags to select the behaviour: `isPromoted`, `isTransfered`, `isKpostIDRequired`, `isMapped`. `requestType` defaults to `allocate` and also accepts `promote`, `reallocate`, `suspend`, `terminate` and `revoked` (see `KPOSTConstants`).

Assign an employee to a vacancy.description: Assign an employee to a vacancy

Promote to a new HR position.description: Promote to a new HR position

200.description: `value` is the updated `RolePostingEntity`, including any newly issued `kpostID`.

500.description: The service returned nothing — commonly no document matching the `id` — or the write / outbound integration threw. **No `error` key is set on this endpoint**, so both cases look identical from the client's side.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or a type mismatch on `countryCode` / `countryId` (integers), `ksmaccCompanyID` (long) or `rejoiningDate`.

post.summary: Suspend, terminate, revoke or reinstate an employee
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the employee lifecycle action. Drives suspension (temporary, with a `duration` and an expected `rejoiningDate`), termination (permanent), revocation, and reinstatement, selected by `requestType`.

**Acting administrator is taken from the token.** Before doing anything the controller overwrites `adminKsmaccID` with the `kpostID` request attribute injected by the JWT filter. Whatever you send in that field is discarded — the action is always attributed to the authenticated caller, which is what makes the audit trail trustworthy.

**Database behaviour** — updates the matching document(s) in `table_admin_role_posting`, flipping `active_status` and recording `reason`, `remarks`, `duration` and `rejoining_date`. **Nothing is deleted** — the seat and its history remain.

**Side effects — reaches beyond MongoDB.** The service issues outbound calls to the KSMACC/KPOST platforms so the employee's access is suspended or revoked there too. Those calls are not transactional with the MongoDB write: a failure can leave the local record updated while the remote system is not, so verify with `getSuspendOrTerminateEmployee` after an error.

**Reinstatement is also automatic** — a scheduler scans for postings whose `rejoining_date` has arrived (`findByRejoiningDateBetween`) and reactivates them without an API call.

**`requestType` values** — `suspend`, `terminate`, `revoked`, `reallocate`, `promote` (see `KPOSTConstants`).

Audited as `rolePosting/suspendOrTerminateEmployee`.

requestBody.description: `companyId`, `employeeId` and `requestType` are the essentials. For a suspension add `duration` and `rejoiningDate`; `reason` and `remarks` are recorded on the posting for the audit trail in every case. **Do not bother sending `adminKsmaccID`** — it is overwritten from the authenticated caller's token.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or `rejoiningDate` not in `yyyy-MM-dd` form (it binds to `java.sql.Date`).

500.description: The service returned anything other than `SUCCESS` — an unknown `requestType`, no matching posting, or an invalid state transition — or the write / outbound integration threw. Re-read the posting before retrying, since the local update may already have been applied.

200.description: Action applied. `value` is the literal string `SUCCESS`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — retires a seat while keeping the record for audit and reporting. Prefer this over `delete` whenever the posting has ever been occupied.

**Database behaviour** — updates rather than removes the document in `table_admin_role_posting`, marking it inactive. Consult `RolePostingSetUpServiceImpl.softDelete` for exactly which fields are flipped — the posting continues to be returned by reads that do not filter on `active_status`.

**Side effects** — the posting disappears from active listings but remains in the collection and in any mapping tables. Reversible by flipping the flag back. Audited as `rolePosting/softDelete`.

**Cosmetic quirk** — the response's `urlPath` is hardcoded to `delete`, not `softDelete`. Do not use it to tell the two operations apart in logs.

requestBody.description: The posting to retire, identified by its `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`).

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the write threw.

200.description: Posting soft-deleted. `value` is the literal string `SUCCESS`; `urlPath` reads `delete`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the main provisioning call. Creates one or more seats in the organisation, optionally filling each with an employee in the same request.

**Database behaviour** — for each request element the service resolves the workplace and HR hierarchy paths, composes the `*_json` snapshots, checks for an existing seat at the same location/HR-variable combination (`existsByWorkplaceLocationIdAndLastHrVariableId`) and writes to `table_admin_role_posting`. When `isKpostIDRequired` is set, a KPOST identifier is generated and stamped onto the posting.

**Side effects — this operation reaches beyond MongoDB.** Depending on the request flags it may call out to the KSMACC/KPOST services to register the employee and obtain a `kpostID`, and it may write mapping records. It is **not transactional**: if an outbound call fails partway through the array, earlier postings remain saved. Retrying a failed batch can therefore create duplicates — reconcile with `getRolePostingByCompanyId` first.

**Result shape** — `value` is an array of `RolePostingResponseDTO`, one per input element. Each carries `savedEntities` (the postings written) and a `statusMessage`; elements that were skipped — a duplicate seat, for instance — come back with an explanatory `statusMessage` and no `savedEntities`. **A `200` therefore does not mean every element succeeded** — inspect each DTO.

Audited as `rolePosting/save`.

requestBody.description: Array of role posting requests. Per element the essentials are `companyId`, the workplace anchor (`lastWorkplaceTierId`, `lastWorkplaceVariableId`, `workplaceLocationId`) and the HR anchor (`lastHrTierId`, `lastHrVariableId`). Include `employeeId` to fill the seat immediately, or leave it null to create a vacancy. `workplaceLocationId` is a **list** on this request object even though the stored posting holds a single value.

200.description: `value` is the array of per-element `RolePostingResponseDTO` results. Check each element's `statusMessage` — `saved` indicates success, anything else explains why that element was not written.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a type mismatch — `countryCode` and `countryId` are integers, and `rejoiningDate` is a SQL date string (`yyyy-MM-dd`).

500.description: The service returned an empty list (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write / outbound integration threw. Because the batch is not transactional, postings created before the failure are still persisted.

post.summary: List currently suspended or terminated employees
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the review screen for employees who are not currently active: who is suspended, why, and when they are due back.

**Database behaviour** — queries `table_admin_role_posting` for the company's postings with `active_status: false` (`findByEmployeeIdIsNotNullAndCompanyIdAndActiveStatus`) and projects each into a `SuspendOrTerminateResponseObject`, joining employee details from `table_admin_employee_details` in Java.

**Unusual status handling — read carefully.** This method returns **HTTP `200 OK` in both branches**. When the list is empty the body still says `200 OK` at the HTTP level but the envelope carries `status: FAILURE`, `statusCode: 500` and `error: "Status is Empty"`. An empty result is normal (nobody is suspended), so treat that specific `error` value as "no rows", not as a fault.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`rolePosting/getSuspendOrTerminateEmployee`).

requestBody.description: `companyId` is required; `requestType` may narrow the listing to suspensions or terminations.

200.description:
Returned on both outcomes:

* **Rows found** — `value` is the array of `SuspendOrTerminateResponseObject`, `status: SUCCESS`, `statusCode: 200`.
* **No rows** — no `value` key; `status: FAILURE`, `statusCode: 500` and `error: "Status is Empty"`, despite the HTTP `200`.

500.description: An actual read failure — reached only when the query itself throws. `error` carries the driver message.

post.summary: Fetch a single role posting by id
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — loads one seat into an edit or detail view, with its hierarchy path snapshots and any transient enrichment the service attaches.

**Database behaviour** — a direct primary-key lookup (`findById`) against `table_admin_role_posting`. All body fields other than `id` are ignored.

**Not-found behaviour** — an `id` that matches no document is **not** a `404`: the response is `200 OK` with `value: null` and `status: SUCCESS`. Check for `null` explicitly.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`rolePosting/getRolePostingById`).

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the posting to fetch.

500.description: The read threw — most often an `id` that is not a valid 24-character hex `ObjectId`.

200.description: `value` is the `RolePostingEntity`, or `null` when no document matches the `id`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the main org-chart / seat listing for a tenant, covering both filled seats and vacancies.

**Database behaviour** — queries `table_admin_role_posting` on `company_id`, narrowing further from whichever optional fields the request object carries. The repository backs several shapes — by company alone, by company and workplace location, by company and active status, and by company and HR variable — and `RolePostingSetUpServiceImpl.getRolePostingByCompanyId` selects among them. Each returned posting is then enriched in Java with transient values such as `locationName` and `employeeDetails`, which costs additional reads per posting.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`rolePosting/getRolePostingByCompanyId`).

requestBody.description: `companyId` is required. Add `workplaceLocaID` or `lastHrVariableId` to narrow the listing to one location or HR position; leave them null for every posting in the company.

500.description: One of the reads threw, or enrichment hit a dangling reference. `error` carries the message.

200.description: `value` is the array of `RolePostingEntity` documents with transient enrichment applied; `[]` when nothing matches.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — answers "which seat(s) does this person hold?". Used by the employee detail view and before a transfer or promotion, to establish the current position.

**Database behaviour** — a derived query `findByEmployeeIdAndCompanyIdAndActiveStatus` over `table_admin_role_posting`, matching the employee within the company. An employee can legitimately hold more than one posting, hence the array return.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`rolePosting/getRolePostingByCompanyIdAndEmployeeId`).

requestBody.description: `companyId` and `employeeId` are both required. `employeeId` is the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of a `table_admin_employee_details` document.

200.description: `value` is the array of postings held by that employee; `[]` when the employee holds none.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

post.summary: List employees under an HR node with their reporting chain (KAMS)
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — **built for the KAMS construction project set-up module.** When KAMS assembles a project team it needs everyone sitting at a given HR position together with each person's reporting line, so approvals can be routed correctly.

**Database behaviour** — a multi-collection read. `findByCompanyIdAndLastHrVariableId` over `table_admin_role_posting` finds the postings at the requested HR node; for each, employee names are resolved from `table_admin_employee_details` and the reporting chain is expanded from the posting's `reporting_hr_json` snapshot into a list of `ReportingPersonDto`. All joins happen in Java, so cost grows with team size.

**Result shape** — `value` is an array of **`KamsAssignProjectTeamResponseObject`**, each carrying `employeeId`, `firstName`, `lastName`, the raw `reportingHrJson` and the expanded `reportingPersons` list.

**Snapshot caveat** — `reportingHrJson` was captured when the posting was written. If the HR hierarchy has since been re-parented, the chain returned here reflects the structure as it stood then, not as it stands now.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`rolePosting/getEmployeeDetailsByLastHrvariableId`).

requestBody.description: `companyId` and `lastHrVariableId` are required. `lastHrVariableId` is the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of a node in `table_admin_hr_setup_tier_variable`.

200.description: `value` is the array of `KamsAssignProjectTeamResponseObject`; `[]` when no posting sits at that HR node.

500.description: One of the reads threw, or a stored `reporting_hr_json` snapshot could not be parsed — a malformed or truncated value will surface here. `error` carries the message.

post.summary: List a company's employees for lifecycle actions
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — populates the employee picker on the suspend / terminate / reallocate screens. It returns a flattened, action-oriented projection rather than raw postings.

**Database behaviour** — reads occupied postings for the company from `table_admin_role_posting` (`findByEmployeeIdIsNotNullAndCompanyId…`) and maps each into a `SuspendOrTerminateResponseObject`, resolving the employee's name, contact details and PAN from `table_admin_employee_details` into the nested `employeeDetails` block. The join is performed in Java.

**Result shape** — `value` is an array of **`SuspendOrTerminateResponseObject`**, not of `RolePostingEntity`. It carries the current `activeStatus`, `reason`, `remarks`, `duration` and `rejoiningDate` so the UI can show existing suspensions inline.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`rolePosting/getEmployeeByCompanyId`).

**Data-protection note** — includes each employee's mobile, e-mail and PAN number.

requestBody.description: `companyId` is required; other fields on the request object may further narrow the listing.

200.description: `value` is the array of `SuspendOrTerminateResponseObject` projections; `[]` when the company has no occupied postings.

500.description: One of the reads threw, or projection hit a dangling `employee_id`. `error` carries the message.

post.summary: List filled role postings plus the company administrator
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — renders the "who works here" view: every seat that actually has someone in it, alongside the company administrator's own profile so the UI can show both in one screen without a second call.

**Database behaviour** — two reads against two collections. First `findByEmployeeIdIsNotNullAndCompanyId…` over `table_admin_role_posting` returns the occupied seats; then `AdminDetailsService.findByCompanyId` fetches the administrator from `table_admin_details`.

**Two top-level keys.** Unlike every other endpoint, the response carries the postings under `value` **and** the administrator under a separate **`admin`** key. Clients written against the standard envelope will miss the administrator entirely.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`rolePosting/getAssignedRolePostingEmployeeByCompanyId`).

requestBody.description: `companyId` is required — it scopes both the posting listing and the administrator lookup.

200.description: `value` holds the occupied postings; `admin` holds the company's `AdminDetailsEntity` (or `null` if none is on file).

500.description: Either read threw. `error` carries the message.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes a seat created in error. For an employee who is leaving or being suspended use `suspendOrTerminateEmployee` (which preserves history) or `softDelete`; this operation destroys the record.

**Database behaviour** — a hard delete against `table_admin_role_posting`. The document and its `*_json` history snapshots are physically removed with no recovery path.

**Side effects** — destructive and not cascading. Rows in `table_admin_role_employee_mapping` and `table_product_employee_mapping` that reference this posting keep a dangling `role_posting_id`. The repository exposes `existsByIdAndEmployeeIdIsNotNull` — check that the seat is vacant before deleting. Audited as `rolePosting/delete`.

requestBody.description: The posting to delete, identified by its `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`).

200.description: Posting deleted. `value` is the literal string `SUCCESS`.

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — no matching document, or a guard refusing to delete an occupied seat — or the delete threw.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — administrative seeding of the project catalogue in one call, typically at deployment time or when a new KPOST offering is launched.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces documents in `table_admin_project_details`, one per array element. Elements carrying an `id` replace that document wholesale; elements without one are inserted with a generated `ObjectId`. Projects already stored and omitted from the payload are left untouched.

**Side effects** — the catalogue is global, so a write here is visible to every tenant. An audit entry (`project/saveAllProject`) is written before the attempt.

requestBody.description: Array of project documents. `title` is the display name, `abbreviation` the short code used as a cross-module reference, and `content` free-form descriptive copy. Omit `id` to insert.

example.title: KPOST Asset Management System
example.content: Construction asset and project team management.

example.title: KPOST Human Resources
example.content: Employee lifecycle, hierarchy and role posting.

500.description: The service returned an empty list (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the bulk write threw. A partial failure mid-array is not rolled back.

200.description: `value` is the array of persisted `ProjectDetailsEntity` documents, each with its `id` populated.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a field has the wrong type.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — grants a company access to a catalogue product after a sale or renewal.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces a single document in `table_product_purchase`. Omit `id` to insert with a generated `ObjectId`; supply an existing `id` to replace that subscription in full (the renewal path). `subscription_date` defaults to the current timestamp unless you send one.

**No duplicate guard** — nothing prevents two active subscriptions for the same company/product pair. Look the existing one up and replace it by `id` rather than inserting a second.

**Side effects** — immediately changes what the tenant sees as purchased on `productMaster/productList/{companyId}`. Audited as `productPurchase/save`.

requestBody.description: The subscription to record. `productId` is the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of a `table_product_master` document; `companyId` is the business tenant identifier. Omit `subscriptionDate` to accept the current timestamp. `endDate` is stored but not enforced.

500.description: The service returned nothing (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or a date field that Jackson cannot parse into `java.util.Date`.

200.description: `value` is the persisted `ProductPurchase` including its generated `id` and defaulted `subscriptionDate`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — administrative seeding of the product catalogue, typically at deployment time or when a new KPOST product is launched.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces documents in `table_product_master`, one per array element. Elements carrying an `id` replace that document in full; the rest are inserted with a generated `ObjectId`. Products already stored and omitted from the payload are left untouched.

**Side effects** — the catalogue is global, so a write here changes what **every** tenant sees on its product page. Audited as `productMaster/save`.

requestBody.description: Array of product documents. `productCode` is the stable cross-module identifier and should be unique. `productLogo` is typically a URL or a base64 data URI. Do not send `isPurchased` or `productPurchase` — both are `@Transient` and are discarded on write.

example.productDescription: Construction asset and project team management.

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS`, or the bulk write threw. Partial writes are not rolled back.

200.description: All products persisted. `value` is the literal string `SUCCESS`.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a field has the wrong type.

post.summary: License employees to a product in bulk
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — assigns a batch of employees access to a product the company has purchased, typically from the "manage product users" screen.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces documents in `table_product_employee_mapping`, one per array element (`saveAll`). Elements carrying an `id` replace that mapping; the rest are inserted with a generated `ObjectId`.

**No duplicate guard** — re-sending the same employee/product pair without an `id` creates a second mapping rather than updating the first, so a retried request double-licenses the employee. De-duplicate before sending.

**Side effects** — grants product access; downstream KPOST services resolve entitlement through these records. Audited as `productEmployeeMapping/save`.

requestBody.description: Array of licensing records. Per element supply `companyId`, `productId` (the `ObjectId` of a `table_product_master` document) and `employeeId`. `rolePostingId` and `kpostId` tie the licence to the employee's posting and cross-system identity; none of the references is validated to exist.

200.description: `value` is the array of persisted mappings with their generated `id`s.

500.description: The service returned an empty list (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the bulk write threw. Partial writes are not rolled back.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a field has the wrong type.

post.summary: Attach a KPOST ID to a mapping (KAMS integration)
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — **called by the KAMS service**, not by the Admin UI. KAMS writes back the `kpostId` it has issued for an employee so that subsequent entitlement lookups can resolve the cross-system identity.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces a single document in `table_product_employee_mapping`. Supply the existing mapping's `id` to update it in place; omit `id` and a **new** mapping document is created instead of the intended one being amended.

**Two things differ from every other endpoint in this module:**

* It is the only route named explicitly in the security configuration's permit list, so it is reachable without the usual token — treat it as a machine-to-machine contract and restrict it at the network layer.
* It takes **no** `HttpServletRequest` and writes **no audit entry**. Calls here leave no trace in the audit collection.

**Side effects** — changes cross-system identity resolution for the employee.

requestBody.description: The mapping to write. Include the existing `id` to amend a mapping in place — omitting it creates a new document. `kpostId` is the cross-system identity being recorded.

500.description: The service returned nothing (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

200.description: `value` is the persisted mapping document including its `id` and `kpostId`.

post.summary: List the role postings licensed to a product
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — shows who currently has access to a product, rendered with full posting context (hierarchy path, location, display name) rather than bare ids.

**Database behaviour** — a two-collection read. The service first queries `table_product_employee_mapping` with `find({ "companyId": …, "productId": … })`, then resolves each mapping's employee into the matching document from `table_admin_role_posting`. The join happens in Java, not via a `$lookup` aggregation, so cost grows with the number of licensed employees.

**Return type note** — `value` is an array of **`RolePostingEntity`**, not of `ProductEmployeeMapping`.

**Empty result is reported as a failure** — when no employee is licensed to the product, the response is `500` with `status: FAILURE` and no `error` key, not an empty `200`. Handle that case explicitly.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`productEmployeeMapping/getMappedEmployeeByCompanyIdAndProductId`).

requestBody.description: Only `productId` (24-character hex `ObjectId`) and `companyId` are read.

200.description: `value` is the array of `RolePostingEntity` documents for the licensed employees.

500.description: Either **no employees are licensed** to that product (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key — the common case, and not a server fault), or one of the reads threw, in which case `error` carries the message.

post.summary: Resolve the KPOST IDs licensed to a product
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the lightweight identity-only variant of `getMappedEmployeeByCompanyIdAndProductId`. **Consumed by the KPOST service** to look up company details from a product id (integration added 28 Oct 2025).

**Database behaviour** — queries `table_product_employee_mapping` with `find({ "companyId": …, "productId": … })` and projects only the `kpostId` field into a list of strings — no join against role postings or employee details, so it is considerably cheaper than the sibling read.

**Non-standard response key.** The identifiers are returned under **`kpostIDs`**, not under the usual `value` key. Clients written against the standard envelope will find `value` absent.

**Empty result is reported as a failure** — when nothing is licensed the response is `500` with `status: FAILURE`, not an empty `200`.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`productEmployeeMapping/getKpostIDsByCompanyIdAndProductId`).

requestBody.description: Only `productId` (24-character hex `ObjectId`) and `companyId` are read.

200.description: The `kpostIDs` key holds the array of KPOST identity strings. There is no `value` key on this endpoint.

500.description: Either no KPOST IDs are mapped to that product (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the read threw.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — corrects a site's address, renames it, moves it to a different hierarchy node, or re-points its reporting site.

**Database behaviour** — replaces the document identified by `id` in `table_admin_location`. Whole-document write: fields omitted from the body are persisted as `null`, so send the complete location rather than a patch.

**Side effects** — role postings anchored to this location by `workplace_location_id` keep working and immediately reflect the new address. Other locations naming this one in `reportingWorkplaceLocationId` are unaffected. Audited as `location/update`.

requestBody.description: Complete location document including the `id` to update. Omitted fields are written as `null`.

200.description: `value` is the updated location document.

500.description: No document matched the supplied `id` (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

400.description: Malformed JSON body, or a type mismatch on `countryId`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — registers a batch of physical sites during company set-up or when a region is expanded.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces documents in `table_admin_location`, one per array element. Elements without an `id` are inserted with a generated `ObjectId`; elements carrying an `id` replace that document in full. The service derives `abbreviation` and `code` and checks them against the existing collection (`existsByAbbreviation` / `existsByCode`) so they stay unique.

**Side effects** — locations saved here become assignable on role postings. Nothing validates `attributeId`, `variableId` or `reportingWorkplaceLocationId` against live documents. Audited as `location/save`.

requestBody.description: Array of location documents. Supply `companyId`, `attributeId`, `variableId` and `locationName` at minimum. Address fields can be pre-filled from `country/getAddressUsingPincode`. `countryId` is an **integer**.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a field has the wrong type — note `countryId` is a numeric `int`, not a string.

200.description: `value` is the array of persisted locations with `id`, `abbreviation` and `code` populated.

500.description: The service returned an empty list (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the bulk write threw. Partial writes are not rolled back.

post.summary: Resolve the sites reporting to a location
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — renders the reporting branch beneath a site: which other locations name this one as their reporting parent.

**Database behaviour** — runs the repository's `@Query`-annotated **case-insensitive regular-expression** match `{ 'reportingWorkplaceLocation': { $regex: <id>, $options: 'i' } }` over `table_admin_location`, and projects the hits into loose key/value maps rather than full entities.

**Performance and correctness caveats worth knowing:**

* A `$regex` that is not left-anchored **cannot use an index** — this is a collection scan, and it degrades as the location count grows.
* Because it is a substring match, an id that happens to appear inside a longer value will also match. Treat the result as approximate.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`location/getReportingLocationName`).

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the location whose reporting children should be listed.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw — a scan timeout on a large collection, or an `id` containing characters that break the regular expression.

200.description: `value` is an array of untyped maps describing the reporting locations; `[]` when nothing reports to this site.

post.summary: List locations sitting at a hierarchy node
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — shows which physical sites belong to a selected node of the workplace hierarchy, for example every office under *Chennai Zone*.

**Database behaviour** — a derived query `find({ "attributeId": <attributeId>, "variableId": <variableId> })` over `table_admin_location`. Both fields come from the request body.

**Scope warning** — this query is **not filtered by `companyId`**. If two tenants ever share an `attributeId`/`variableId` pair the results would cross tenant boundaries. In practice the ids are Mongo `ObjectId`s and therefore globally unique, but do not rely on this endpoint for tenant isolation — prefer `getAllLocation`, which does filter by company.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`location/getLocation`).

requestBody.description: Only `attributeId` and `variableId` are read — both 24-character hex `ObjectId`s identifying the hierarchy node.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

200.description: `value` is the array of locations at that node; `[]` when none match.

post.summary: Fetch a single location by id
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — loads one site into an edit form, or resolves the full address behind a `workplace_location_id` held on a role posting.

**Database behaviour** — a direct primary-key lookup (`findById`) against `table_admin_location`. All body fields other than `id` are ignored.

**Not-found behaviour** — an unmatched `id` returns `200 OK` with `value: null` and `status: SUCCESS`, not a `404`.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`location/getLocationById`).

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the location to fetch.

200.description: `value` is the location document, or `null` when no document matches the `id`.

500.description: The read threw — most often an `id` that is not a valid 24-character hex `ObjectId`.

post.summary: List a company's locations under a node and reporting site
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the tenant-safe location read. Narrows sites by hierarchy node **and** reporting parent, which is what the location tree view needs when drilling into a reporting branch.

**Database behaviour** — a three-field derived query `find({ "variableId": …, "reportingWorkplaceLocationId": …, "companyId": … })` over `table_admin_location`. All three are exact equality matches — an omitted field is matched against `null` rather than ignored, so leaving one out narrows the result set instead of widening it.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`location/getAllLocation`).

requestBody.description: Only `variableId`, `reportingWorkplaceLocationId` and `companyId` are read. All three participate in the filter — pass `null` deliberately if you mean "stored as null", not as "any value".

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

200.description: `value` is the array of matching locations; `[]` when the three-way filter matches nothing.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes a site that was closed or created in error.

**Database behaviour** — `delete(id)` against `table_admin_location`. A hard delete: the document is physically removed with no soft-delete flag.

**Side effects** — destructive. Role postings anchored to this site keep a dangling `workplace_location_id`, and other locations naming it in `reportingWorkplaceLocationId` lose their reporting target. `rolePosting` exposes `existsByWorkplaceLocationId` internally — check for dependent postings before deleting. Audited as `location/delete`.

**Response note** — the success envelope carries no `value` key; branch on `status`.

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the location to delete.

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the delete threw.

200.description: Location deleted. Envelope carries `status: SUCCESS` and `statusCode: 200` but no `value`.
