**Side effects** — changing `parentVariableId` moves the node's subtree implicitly, since children are resolved by parent id. Audited as `hrVariable/update`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — adds one value to an HR level, for example a new grade within a band.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces a single document in `table_admin_hr_variable`. Omit `id` to insert with a generated `ObjectId`; supply an existing `id` to replace that document in full. The service derives `abbreviation` and `code` from `variable_name`.

**Note** — this takes one object, **not** an array. Sending a JSON array here produces a `400`, unlike `hrSetUpTierVariable/save` and `variable/save` which expect arrays.

**Side effects** — nothing validates `attributeId` or `parentVariableId` against existing documents. Audited as `hrVariable/save`.

requestBody.description: A single HR variable. Supply `companyId`, `attributeId` (the HR level this value belongs to) and `variableName`. Leave `parentVariableId` and `parentAttributeId` null for a root value.

500.description: The service returned nothing (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

200.description: `value` is the persisted variable with `id`, `abbreviation` and `code` populated.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or a JSON array was sent where a single object is expected.

post.summary: List the direct children of an HR variable
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — lazy expansion of the HR tier tree as the user drills down.

**Database behaviour** — a two-field derived query `find({ "parent_variable_id": <parentVariableId>, "company_id": <companyId> })` over `table_admin_hr_variable`. Only direct children are returned.

**Root nodes** — pass `parentVariableId` as `null` to list the top of the tree.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`hrVariable/getVariable`).

requestBody.description: Only `parentVariableId` (24-character hex `ObjectId`, or `null` for roots) and `companyId` are read.

200.description: `value` is the array of direct child variables; `[]` for a leaf node or an unknown parent.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes a value from the HR tier.

**Database behaviour** — a hard delete against `table_admin_hr_variable`. The document is physically removed; there is no soft-delete flag.

**Side effects** — destructive and not cascading. Child variables keep pointing at the deleted `parent_variable_id` and drop out of the tree walk. Delete leaves first or re-parent the children. Audited as `hrVariable/delete`.

**Response note** — the success envelope carries no `value` key; branch on `status`.

requestBody.description: The variable to delete, identified by its `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`).

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the delete threw.

200.description: Variable deleted. Envelope carries `status: SUCCESS` and `statusCode: 200` but no `value`.

**Side effects** — HR variables referencing this level by `attributeId` keep their link. Note that `hr_json` strings already stamped onto existing role postings are **snapshots** and are not rewritten, so historical postings keep the old level name. Audited as `hrTier/update`.

requestBody.description: Complete HR level document including the `id` to update. Omitted fields are written as `null`.

post.summary: Create HR hierarchy levels in bulk

post.summary: List all HR hierarchy levels for a company
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the primary read for the HR hierarchy builder: fetches every level a tenant has defined so the ladder can be rendered.

**Database behaviour** — a derived-query `find({ "company_id": <companyId> })` over `table_admin_hr_tier`. Index `company_id` if the collection grows; without one this is a full scan.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`hrTier/getAttributeByCompanyId`).

requestBody.description: Only `companyId` is read — the business tenant identifier, not a Mongo `ObjectId`.

200.description: `value` is the array of HR levels for that company. An unknown `companyId` returns `[]` with `status: SUCCESS` — indistinguishable from a company that has defined none.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

post.summary: Create HR set-up nodes in bulk

post.summary: Resolve an HR node's reporting parent
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — answers "who does this HR position report to?". The result feeds the `reporting_hr_json` value stamped onto role postings and the escalation path shown in the UI.

**Database behaviour** — starts from the node identified by `id` in `table_admin_hr_setup_tier_variable` and follows its `reporting_variable_id` link. This is an application-side lookup, **not** a `$graphLookup` aggregation.

**Shape note** — despite the plural name, this operation returns a **single node** object, not an array, unlike its workplace-tier counterpart `adminTierVariable/getAllReportingVariableHierarchy` which returns a list. Do not assume the two are interchangeable.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`hrSetUpTierVariable/getAllReportingHrTierVariableHierarchy`).

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the node whose reporting parent should be resolved.

200.description: `value` is a single HR node object — the reporting parent — or `null` when the node reports to nobody.

500.description: The lookup threw — a malformed `id`, or a dangling `reporting_variable_id` left by a deleted node.

**Database behaviour** — a derived-query `find({ "company_id": <companyId> })` over `table_admin_hr_setup_tier_attribute`. Index `company_id` if the collection grows.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`hrSetUpTierAttribute/getAttributeByCompanyId`).

requestBody.description: Only `companyId` is read — the business tenant identifier, not a Mongo `ObjectId`.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

200.description: `value` is the array of levels for that company; `[]` when none are defined or the `companyId` is unknown.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes a level created in error or retired from the structure.

**Database behaviour** — a hard delete against `table_admin_hr_setup_tier_attribute`. The document is physically removed; there is no soft-delete flag.

**Side effects** — destructive and not cascading. HR set-up variables still referencing the deleted `attribute_id` are orphaned, and role postings whose `last_hr_tier_id` points here keep a dangling reference that the reporting-chain walk cannot resolve. Verify the level is unused first. Audited as `hrSetUpTierAttribute/delete`.

requestBody.description: The level to delete, identified by its `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`).

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the delete threw.

200.description: Level deleted. `value` is the literal string `SUCCESS`.

post.summary: Add a holiday to the calendar
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the HR administrator declares a public or company holiday. Downstream leave and attendance features read the resulting calendar.

**Database behaviour** — inserts a document into `table_holiday` after the service checks for an existing entry on the same date for the same company/scope. A duplicate is **rejected**, not overwritten: the service returns nothing and the response is `500` with `message: "Holiday already exists"`.

**Side effects** — changes the working-day calendar for the company. Audited as `holiday/addHoliday` (note the audit key differs from the route, which is `saveHoliday`).

requestBody.description: Holiday to add. `companyID` scopes it to the tenant; `countryId` and `stateName` narrow it to a region — leave them null for a company-wide holiday. `repeatType` is `0` for the current year or `1` for next year. `date` is an ISO local date (`yyyy-MM-dd`).

500.description:
Two distinct cases, distinguishable by the `message` key:

* **Duplicate** — `message: "Holiday already exists"`, `status: FAILURE`, no `error` key. The calendar is unchanged.
* **Write failure** — no `message`, but `error` carries the exception text.

200.description: `value` is the stored `HolidayEntity` including its generated `id`.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or `date` not in ISO `yyyy-MM-dd` form, or a non-integer `repeatType`.

post.summary: Bind an employee to a role posting
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — records that a specific employee now occupies a specific role posting, creating the audit-friendly link between the two.

**Database behaviour** — inserts a document into `table_admin_role_employee_mapping`. `created_date` is set to today by the entity default unless you supply one. Omit `id` to insert with a generated `ObjectId`.

**No uniqueness guard** — nothing prevents the same `employee_id`/`role_posting_id` pair being written twice, so a retried request creates a duplicate mapping. Check before re-sending, or de-duplicate on read.

**Side effects** — creates a persistent assignment record. Note this does **not** update `table_admin_role_posting` itself; to set the posting's own `employee_id` use `rolePosting/update`. Audited as `employeeRoleMapping/save`.

requestBody.description: The mapping to create. `companyId` is the tenant scope; `employeeId` and `rolePostingId` are 24-character hex `ObjectId`s pointing at `table_admin_employee_details` and `table_admin_role_posting` respectively — neither is validated to exist. Omit `createdDate` to accept today's date.

200.description: `value` holds whatever the service returned — normally the persisted mapping document with its generated `id`. Note this method has no failure branch, so a `null` service result is still reported as `status: SUCCESS` with `value: null`.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or `createdDate` not in ISO `yyyy-MM-dd` form.

500.description: The MongoDB insert threw. `error` carries the driver message.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — amends an existing profile: an address change, a new qualification, a corrected mobile number.

**Database behaviour** — updates the document identified by `id` in `table_admin_employee_details`.

**Send the whole document.** Sub-documents are replaced, not merged — posting an `educationObj` array with one entry discards any others already stored, and omitting a sub-document entirely risks nulling it. Read the current record first, mutate it, then send it back.

**Side effects** — role postings bound to this employee by `employee_id` are not modified, but every screen that resolves the employee immediately shows the new values. Audited as `employeeDetails/update`.

requestBody.description: Complete employee document including the `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`) of the record to update. Include every sub-document you wish to retain.

200.description: `value` is the updated `EmployeeDetailsEntity`.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or a type mismatch inside one of the embedded sub-documents.

500.description: No document matched the supplied `id` (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — onboarding: captures a new joiner's full profile in one call, before or alongside assigning them a role posting.

**Database behaviour** — inserts a document into `table_admin_employee_details` with all sub-documents embedded inline. Omit `id` to insert with a generated `ObjectId`; supplying an existing `id` replaces that document in full, so use `employeeDetails/update` for edits.

**Side effects** — creates the record that role postings later bind to via `employee_id`. Audited as `employeeDetails/save`.

requestBody.description: Full employee document. `companyId` is the tenant scope that the read path filters on and is effectively mandatory. Every sub-document is optional at the schema level — nothing is validated server-side — but `personalInformationObj` and `employmentObj` are what the UI relies on. Address blocks can be pre-filled from `country/getAddressUsingPincode`.

500.description: The service returned nothing (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

200.description: `value` is the persisted `EmployeeDetailsEntity` including the generated `id`.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or a type mismatch — most often `personalInformationObj.disability`, which is a boolean rather than a string.

post.summary: List employees by transfer or promotion status
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — drives the transfer and promotion worklists: which employees are flagged as being moved between locations, or elevated to a new designation.

**Database behaviour** — the filter is assembled from the submitted key/value map by `EmployeeDetailsServiceImpl` and applied to `table_admin_employee_details`, matching against the `promotionDetails` / `transferDetails` fields alongside the company scope. Because the request is an untyped `Map<String, String>` rather than a DTO, the accepted keys are defined by that implementation, not by this signature — check it before relying on a key that is not documented here.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`employeeDetails/getTransferOrPromotionDetails`).

requestBody.description: Flat map of **string** filter criteria — not a typed DTO. `companyId` scopes the query; the remaining keys select the worklist. The authoritative key set lives in `EmployeeDetailsServiceImpl.getTransferOrPromotionDetails`.

500.description: A required key was absent from the map, or the read threw. `error` carries the message.

200.description: `value` is the array of matching employee documents; `[]` when nothing matches.

400.description: Body is not a flat JSON object of string values.

post.summary: List all employees of a company
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the employee directory / master grid, and the source for employee pickers when creating role postings.

**Database behaviour** — a derived-query `find({ "companyId": <companyId> })` over `table_admin_employee_details`, returning **complete** employee documents including every embedded sub-document. There is no projection, paging or sort, so the payload scales with both headcount and per-employee profile size and can become large for a big tenant.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`employeeDetails/getEmployeeDetails`).

**Data-protection note** — returns full personal data (DOB, contact details, disability status, PAN) for every employee in the company. Restrict to HR-authorised callers.

requestBody.description: Only `companyId` is read — the business tenant identifier, not a Mongo `ObjectId`.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw — on a large tenant most often a cursor timeout.

200.description: `value` is the array of full employee documents; `[]` when the company has none or the `companyId` is unknown.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes a profile created in error. For a departing employee prefer `rolePosting/suspendOrTerminateEmployee`, which preserves history by flipping `active_status` instead of destroying data.

**Database behaviour** — `delete(id)` against `table_admin_employee_details`. A hard delete: the document and every embedded sub-document are physically removed, with no soft-delete flag and no recovery path.

**Side effects** — destructive and not cascading. Role postings and product mappings referencing this `employee_id` keep a dangling reference and will render without a name. Audited as `employeeDetails/delete`.

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the employee record to delete.

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the delete threw.

200.description: Employee deleted. `value` is the fixed message `Employee Deleted SuccessFully!!`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — renames a job title, moves it to another department, or changes its position in the seniority chain.

**Database behaviour** — updates the document identified by `id` in `table_admin_designation`.

**Side effects** — re-pointing `departmentId` moves the title between departments; child designations linked by `parentDesignationId` follow implicitly since nesting is resolved by id. Communication IDs already issued embed the old abbreviation and are not regenerated. Audited as `designation/update`.

requestBody.description: Designation document including the `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`) of the record to update.

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no document matching the `id` — or the write threw. A `null` service result also lands here as a `NullPointerException`.

200.description: Designation updated. `value` is the service status string (`SUCCESS`).

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — saves all the job titles for a department, or for the whole company, in one call during set-up.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces documents in `table_admin_designation`, one per array element. Elements without an `id` are inserted with a generated `ObjectId`; elements carrying an `id` replace that document in full.

**Recommended flow** — call `designation/abbreviationAndCodeCreation` per title first to obtain a collision-free `abbreviation` and `code`, then include them here.

**Side effects** — nothing validates that `departmentId` references a live department, so a stale id silently creates a designation invisible to the department drill-down. Audited as `designation/save`.

requestBody.description: Array of designations. Supply `companyId`, `departmentId` and `designationName` per element. Set `parentDesignationId` to nest a title under a more senior one, or leave it null for a top-level title. `departmentIdList` is a `@Transient` read-side field and is ignored here.

500.description: The service returned an empty list (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the bulk write threw. Partial writes are not rolled back.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a field has the wrong type.

200.description: `value` is the array of persisted designations with their generated `id`s.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — populates the designation picker when the user has selected one or more departments, avoiding a round-trip per department from the client.

**Database behaviour** — **not** a single `$in` query. The controller loops over `departmentIdList` and issues one `find({ "companyId": …, "departmentId": … })` per element against `table_admin_designation`, concatenating the results. Cost grows linearly with the number of departments requested, so keep the list short. Results are returned in request order with no de-duplication — a repeated `departmentId` yields repeated documents.

**Required field** — `departmentIdList` must be present and non-null. A missing list raises a `NullPointerException` on iteration and the endpoint answers `500`.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`designation/getDesignationByCompanyIdAndDepartmentId`).

requestBody.description: Only `companyId` and `departmentIdList` are read. `departmentIdList` is a **required, non-null** array of 24-character hex `ObjectId`s — one query is run per entry.

500.description: `departmentIdList` was absent or null, or one of the reads threw. `error` carries the message.

200.description: `value` is the concatenated array of designations across the requested departments; `[]` when none match.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes a job title created in error or retired from the structure.

**Database behaviour** — `deleteDesignation(id)` against `table_admin_designation`. A hard delete: the document is physically removed with no soft-delete flag.

**Side effects** — destructive and not cascading. Child designations that still carry the deleted `parentDesignationId` are left orphaned, and employee records referencing the title keep a dangling id. Re-home the children first. Audited as `designation/delete`.

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the designation to delete.

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the delete threw. A `null` service result also lands here as a `NullPointerException`.

200.description: Designation deleted. `value` echoes the service status (`SUCCESS`).

post.summary: Generate a unique abbreviation and code for a designation
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — call it **before** `designation/save` to reserve a short form for a job title. Unlike the department equivalent, this generator takes the parent `departmentId` too, because designation codes are composed relative to their department and only need to be unique within it.

**Database behaviour** — derives a candidate abbreviation from `designationName`, then queries `table_admin_designation` (filtered by the supplied `departmentId`) to check for collisions, retrying with a variation until a free pair is found. Read-only: nothing is written, so the pair is **not reserved** — concurrent callers can receive the same values and the clash only appears at `save` time.

**Side effects** — none beyond the audit entry (`designation/abbreviationAndCodeCreation`).

requestBody.description: Only `designationName` and `departmentId` are read. `departmentId` is the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the owning department — the code is scoped to it.

500.description: The generator returned an empty map — typically a blank `designationName` or an unresolvable `departmentId` — or a read threw.

200.description: `value` is a map of generated values, keyed `abbreviation` and `code`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — renames a department or corrects its abbreviation/code.

**Database behaviour** — updates the document identified by `id` in `table_admin_department`.

**Response caveat** — this method has **no failure branch**: whatever string the service returns is placed in `value` and the response is always `200 OK` with `status: SUCCESS`, including when the service reports `FAILURE` or when no document matched the `id`. Inspect the `value` string itself to confirm the update actually happened; do not rely on `status` here.

**Side effects** — designations referencing this department by `departmentId` keep their link and are not modified. Communication IDs already issued embed the **old** abbreviation and are not regenerated. Audited as `department/update`.

requestBody.description: Department document including the `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`) of the record to update.

200.description: Always returned when no exception is thrown. `value` is the service's status string — check it rather than the envelope's `status`, which is hardcoded to `SUCCESS` on this path.

500.description: Only reached when the update threw — for example a malformed `id`. `error` carries the message.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — company set-up saves the full department list in one call.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces documents in `table_admin_department`, one per array element. Elements without an `id` are inserted with a generated `ObjectId`; elements carrying an `id` replace that document in full.

**Recommended flow** — call `department/abbreviationAndCodeCreation` first for each department name to obtain a collision-free `abbreviation` and `code`, then include those values here. Saving without them leaves the fields null and breaks downstream communication-ID generation.

**Side effects** — departments created here become selectable parents for designations. Audited as `department/save`.

requestBody.description: Array of departments. Supply `companyId` and `departmentName` per element, plus the `abbreviation` and `code` previously obtained from `abbreviationAndCodeCreation`.

500.description: The service returned an empty list (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the bulk write threw. Partial writes are not rolled back.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a field has the wrong type.

200.description: `value` is the array of persisted departments with their generated `id`s.

post.summary: List all departments for a company
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — populates department pickers throughout the admin UI and is the first step of the department → designation drill-down.

**Database behaviour** — a derived-query `find({ "companyId": <companyId> })` over `table_admin_department`. Note the field is stored camelCase, not snake_case, because this entity declares no `@Field` mappings.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`department/getDepartmentByCompanyId`).

requestBody.description: Only `companyId` is read — the business tenant identifier, not a Mongo `ObjectId`.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

200.description: `value` is the array of departments; `[]` when the company has none or the `companyId` is unknown.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes a department created in error or dissolved by a reorganisation.

**Database behaviour** — `deleteDepartment(id)` against `table_admin_department`. A hard delete: the document is physically removed with no soft-delete flag.

**Side effects** — destructive and not cascading. Designations that still carry the deleted `departmentId` are left orphaned and will disappear from the department drill-down while remaining in the collection. Delete or re-home the designations first. Audited as `department/delete`.

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the department to delete.

200.description: Department deleted. `value` echoes the service status (`SUCCESS`).

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the delete threw. A `null` service result also lands here as a `NullPointerException`.

post.summary: Generate a unique abbreviation and code for a department name
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — call it **before** `department/save` to reserve a short form for a department. The generated abbreviation and code are what communication IDs and employee identifiers are composed from, so they must not collide within a tenant.

**Database behaviour** — derives a candidate abbreviation from the supplied `departmentName`, then queries `table_admin_department` to check whether that abbreviation or code is already taken, retrying with a variation until a free pair is found. Read-only: nothing is written, so the returned pair is **not reserved** — two concurrent callers can be handed the same values, and the collision only surfaces at `save` time.

**Side effects** — none beyond the audit entry (`department/abbreviationAndCodeCreation`).

requestBody.description: Only `departmentName` is read — the human-readable name to derive a short form from.

500.description: The generator returned an empty map — typically a blank or null `departmentName`, or no free variation left — or a read threw. `status` is `FAILURE`.

200.description: `value` is a map of generated values, keyed `abbreviation` and `code`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the public "Request a demo" form posts here. It records who wants the demo, how to reach them, when they would like it, and which KPOST products they are interested in.

**Database behaviour** — inserts one document into `table_admin_demo_request`. The `demo_status` field is initialised to `pending` by the entity default, so the sales queue picks the record up immediately. `projectList` is stored as an embedded array of product identifiers; `projectDetailsMap` is `@Transient` — it is never persisted and exists only to enrich read responses.

**Side effects** — creates a sales-visible lead and writes an audit entry (`demo/createDemoRequest`). There is no de-duplication, so submitting the form twice creates two documents.

requestBody.description: Lead details. Supply at least `nameOfUser` plus one contact channel (`contactEmailId` or `contactMobileNumber`) — nothing is enforced at the schema level, so an unreachable lead will be accepted. Omit `id` and `status`; both are assigned server-side.

200.description: Request recorded. `value` is the stored `DemoRequestEntity` including the generated `id` and the defaulted `status` of `pending`. Note that this endpoint does not check whether the service returned an entity, so a `null` result would still be reported as `SUCCESS` with `value: null`.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or `preferredDateAndTime` not in ISO-8601 local date-time form (`yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss`). Rejected during deserialisation.

500.description: The MongoDB insert threw. `error` carries the driver message.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — a one-off / administrative seeding call that loads the master list of countries with their ISO codes and telephone dial codes. Client applications read the catalogue through `country/countryList`; this endpoint is what populates it.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces documents in the `table_admin_country` collection, one per array element. Elements carrying an `id` replace that document; elements without one are inserted with a freshly generated `ObjectId`. This is *not* a replace-the-whole-collection operation — countries already present and absent from the payload are left untouched.

**Side effects** — persists reference data visible to every tenant, and writes an audit entry (`country/save`). Because dial codes drive OTP delivery, a bad `dialCode` here propagates into the mobile-verification flow.

requestBody.description: Array of country documents. `countryName`, `dialCode` and `countryCode` should all be supplied — the collection has no schema validation, so blank values are accepted and will surface in client dropdowns.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a field has the wrong type. Handled by Spring before the controller runs.

200.description: All countries persisted. `value` is the literal string `SUCCESS`.

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS`, or the bulk write threw — an unreachable cluster, or an `id` that is not a valid 24-character hex `ObjectId`. Note that a partial failure mid-array is **not** rolled back: earlier documents stay written.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — renames an attribute or re-scopes it to a different company.

**Database behaviour** — replaces the document identified by `id` in `table_admin_attribute`. The save is a whole-document write, so any field omitted from the body is persisted as `null`.

**Side effects** — generic variables referencing this attribute by `attributeId` keep their link and are not modified. Audited as `attribute/update`.

requestBody.description: Complete attribute document including the `id` to update. Omitted fields are written as `null`.

200.description: `value` is the updated attribute document.

500.description: No document matched the supplied `id` (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — defines a company's base attribute names in a single call.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces documents in `table_admin_attribute`, one per array element. Elements without an `id` are inserted with a generated `ObjectId`; elements carrying an `id` replace that document in full.

**Side effects** — attributes saved here become referenceable by generic variables (`variable/save`) via `attributeId`. Audited as `attribute/save`.

requestBody.description: Array of attributes. Each element needs `companyId` (tenant scope — every read path filters on it) and `attributeName`. Omit `id` to insert.

200.description: `value` is the array of persisted attributes with their generated `id`s.

500.description: The service returned an empty list (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the bulk write threw. Partial writes are not rolled back.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a field has the wrong type.

post.summary: Fetch a single attribute by id
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — loads one attribute into an edit form. `POST` is used only because the identifier travels in the request body.

**Database behaviour** — a direct primary-key lookup (`findById`) against `table_admin_attribute` using the `id` from the body. All other body fields are ignored.

**Not-found behaviour** — an `id` that matches no document is **not** a `404`: the response is `200 OK` with `value: null` and `status: SUCCESS`.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`attribute/getAttribute`).

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the attribute to fetch.

200.description: `value` is the attribute document, or `null` when no document matches the `id`.

500.description: The read threw — most often an `id` that is not a valid 24-character hex `ObjectId`. `error` carries the message.

post.summary: List all attributes for a company
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the tenant-scoped read that populates attribute pickers.

**Database behaviour** — a derived-query `find({ "company_id": <companyId> })` over `table_admin_attribute`. Index `company_id` if the collection grows; without one this is a full scan.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`attribute/getAttributeByCompanyId`).

requestBody.description: Only `companyId` is read — the business tenant identifier, not a Mongo `ObjectId`.

200.description: `value` is the array of attributes for that company. An unknown `companyId` returns `[]` with `status: SUCCESS` — it is indistinguishable from a company that has defined none.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes an attribute that is no longer needed.

**Database behaviour** — a hard delete against `table_admin_attribute`. The document is physically removed; there is no soft-delete flag.

**Side effects** — destructive and not cascading. Generic variables that still carry the deleted `attributeId` are left orphaned. Check for dependants before calling. Audited as `attribute/delete`.

requestBody.description: The attribute to delete, identified by its `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`).

200.description: Attribute deleted. `value` is the literal string `SUCCESS`.

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the delete threw.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — renames a node, or re-parents it by changing `parentVariableId` / `parentAttributeId`, or re-points its reporting line.

**Database behaviour** — loads the document identified by `id` from `table_admin_tier_variable` and saves it back. The write replaces the whole document, so any field omitted from the body is persisted as `null` — send the complete node.

**Side effects** — re-parenting moves the node's entire subtree implicitly, because children are found by `parent_variable_id` rather than by an embedded path. Existing role postings that reference this node by id are unaffected but will now resolve to a different position in the tree. Audited as `adminTierVariable/update`.

requestBody.description: Complete node document including the `id` to update. Nothing prevents you from setting `parentVariableId` to the node's own id or to one of its descendants, which would create a cycle the tree walkers cannot terminate on — validate client-side.

200.description: `value` is the updated node document.

500.description: No document matched the supplied `id` (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the write threw.

post.summary: Create workplace hierarchy nodes in bulk
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the hierarchy builder saves a whole sibling group in one call, for example all the zones belonging to a region.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces documents in `table_admin_tier_variable`, one per array element. Elements without an `id` are inserted with a generated `ObjectId`; elements carrying an `id` replace that document in full. The service derives `abbreviation` and `code` from `variable_name`.

**Side effects** — nodes created here become assignable workplace positions on role postings and locations. Nothing validates that `parentVariableId` points at an existing document, so a typo silently produces an orphan node that will not appear under any parent. Audited as `adminTierVariable/save`.

requestBody.description: Array of hierarchy nodes. Per element supply `companyId`, `attributeId` (the level this node sits at) and `variableName`. Set `parentVariableId` and `parentAttributeId` to `null` for root nodes. The `reporting*` fields are optional and only needed when the reporting line differs from the structural parent.

Child nodes with a reporting line.description: Child nodes with a reporting line

200.description: `value` is the array of persisted nodes with `id`, `abbreviation` and `code` populated.

500.description: The service returned an empty list (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the bulk write threw. Partial writes are not rolled back.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a field has the wrong type.

post.summary: Resolve a node's full reporting chain
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — answers "who does this workplace position ultimately report to?". Used when composing the `reporting_workplace_json` stored on a role posting, and for rendering the escalation path in the UI.

**Database behaviour** — walks the `reporting_variable_id` links starting from the node identified by `id`, issuing one `findById` against `table_admin_tier_variable` per hop. This is an application-side traversal, **not** a `$graphLookup` aggregation, so a deep chain costs one round-trip per level.

**Note on the reporting line** — the walk follows `reporting_variable_id`, which is deliberately distinct from `parent_variable_id`: a node's reporting chain need not match its structural ancestry.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`adminTierVariable/getAllReportingVariableHierarchy`).

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the node whose reporting chain should be resolved.

200.description: `value` is the ordered array of nodes forming the reporting chain; `[]` when the node reports to nobody.

500.description: A read during the walk threw — a malformed `id`, or a dangling `reporting_variable_id` left behind by a deleted node. `error` carries the message.

post.summary: List the direct children of a hierarchy node
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — drives lazy expansion in the hierarchy tree view: the client asks for one node's children as the user drills down, rather than loading the whole tree.

**Database behaviour** — a two-field derived query `find({ "parent_variable_id": <parentVariableId>, "company_id": <companyId> })` over `table_admin_tier_variable`. Only **direct** children are returned; grandchildren require another call per level.

**Root nodes** — pass `parentVariableId` as `null` to list the top of the tree, since root documents are stored with a null parent.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`adminTierVariable/getAdminTierVariable`).

requestBody.description: Only `parentVariableId` and `companyId` are read. `parentVariableId` is a 24-character hex `ObjectId`, or `null` to fetch root nodes.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

200.description: `value` is the array of direct child nodes; `[]` for a leaf node or an unknown parent.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes a node from the workplace tree.

**Database behaviour** — a hard delete against `table_admin_tier_variable`. The document is physically removed; there is no soft-delete flag.

**Side effects** — destructive and not cascading. Child nodes keep pointing at the deleted `parent_variable_id` and become unreachable through the tree walk, and locations or role postings referencing the node keep a dangling id. Delete leaves upward, or re-parent the children first. Audited as `adminTierVariable/delete`.

**Response note** — unlike most delete endpoints in this module, the success envelope carries no `value` key; check `status` instead.

requestBody.description: The node to delete, identified by its `id` (24-character hex `ObjectId`).

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the delete threw.

200.description: Node deleted. Envelope carries `status: SUCCESS` and `statusCode: 200` but no `value`.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — renaming a level (say *Branch* to *Site*) after the hierarchy is already in use, without disturbing the variables hanging off it.

**Database behaviour** — loads the document identified by `id` from `table_admin_tier_attribute` and writes the updated document back. Because the entity is saved whole, fields you omit from the body are persisted as `null` — send the complete document, not a patch.

**Side effects** — the renamed level is reflected everywhere the hierarchy is rendered. Variables previously attached to this attribute keep their `attribute_id` reference and are not modified. Audited as `adminTierAttribute/update`.

requestBody.description: Complete attribute document including the `id` of the level to update. Omitted fields are written as `null`.

200.description: `value` is the updated attribute document.

500.description: The service returned nothing — typically because no document matches the supplied `id` (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key) — or the write threw, in which case `error` carries the message.

post.summary: Create workplace hierarchy levels in bulk
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — used during company set-up when the admin defines the whole workplace ladder at once (for example *Region → Zone → Branch*), and later when a new level is introduced.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or replaces documents in `table_admin_tier_attribute`, one per array element. Elements without an `id` are inserted with a generated `ObjectId`; elements carrying an `id` replace that document in full. The service also derives the `abbreviation` and `code` fields from `attribute_name`.

**Side effects** — levels created here become selectable when defining workplace variables and locations, so adding a level changes what the hierarchy builder offers. An audit entry (`adminTierAttribute/save`) is written first.

requestBody.description: Array of hierarchy levels. Supply `companyId` and `attributeName` on every element — `companyId` is the tenant scope that every read path filters on, so an element missing it becomes invisible to the UI. Leave `abbreviation` and `code` out; the service generates them.

200.description: `value` is the array of persisted attributes, each with `id`, `abbreviation` and `code` populated.

500.description: The service returned an empty list (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the bulk write threw. Partial writes are not rolled back.

400.description: Body is not a JSON array, or a field has the wrong type.

post.summary: Fetch a single hierarchy level by id
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — loads one level into an edit form. `POST` is used rather than `GET` only because the identifier travels in the request body.

**Database behaviour** — a direct primary-key lookup (`findById`) against `table_admin_tier_attribute` using the `_id` taken from the request body's `id` field. All other fields in the body are ignored.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`adminTierAttribute/getAttribute`).

**Known defect — read this before integrating.** On the success path this method returns HTTP `500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` while the envelope inside says `status: SUCCESS, statusCode: 200`. The payload is correct; only the HTTP status line is wrong. Clients must therefore branch on the envelope's `status` field, not on the HTTP status code, until the mismatch is fixed.

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the level to fetch. Any other property you send is ignored.

500.description:
Returned on **both** outcomes because of the defect described above:

* **Success** — envelope reads `status: SUCCESS`, `statusCode: 200`, and `value` holds the attribute document. If no document matches the `id`, `value` is `null` and `status` is still `SUCCESS`.
* **Failure** — envelope reads `status: FAILURE` with the exception message in `error`, most often a malformed `id` that is not a valid 24-character hex `ObjectId`.

post.summary: List all hierarchy levels for a company
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the primary read for the workplace hierarchy builder: fetches every level a tenant has defined so the UI can render the ladder and offer the levels for selection.

**Database behaviour** — a derived-query `find({ "company_id": <companyId> })` over `table_admin_tier_attribute`. Add an index on `company_id` if this collection grows; without one the query is a full collection scan.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`adminTierAttribute/getAttributeByCompanyId`).

requestBody.description: Only `companyId` is read — the tenant whose levels should be listed. Note this is the business company identifier, not a Mongo `ObjectId`.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

200.description: `value` is the array of levels for that company. A company that has not defined any levels yields `[]` with `status: SUCCESS` — an unknown `companyId` is indistinguishable from a company with no levels.

post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes a level that was created in error or is no longer part of the tenant's structure.

**Database behaviour** — a hard `deleteById` against `table_admin_tier_attribute`. The document is physically removed; there is no soft-delete flag and no recovery path.

**Side effects** — destructive and not transactional. Workplace variables still referencing the deleted `attribute_id` are **not** cascaded or cleaned up, so removing a level that is still in use leaves orphaned variables that will render without a parent level. Verify the level is unused before calling. Audited as `adminTierAttribute/delete`.

requestBody.description: Only `id` is read — the 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the level to delete.

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly because no document matched the `id` — or the delete threw, in which case `error` carries the message.

200.description: Level deleted. `value` is the literal string `SUCCESS`.

post.summary: Create or replace the company administrator profile
post.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — called during tenant onboarding (and whenever the admin's personal details change) to record who administers the company's Admin Module. Downstream screens read this record to show "managed by" information next to the company's role postings.

**Database behaviour** — performs a `save` against the `table_admin_details` collection. Spring Data decides between insert and replace from the `id` field: send `id` as `null` to insert a new document (Mongo generates the `ObjectId`), or send an existing 24-character hex `id` to overwrite that document *in full*. There is no partial merge — any field you omit is persisted as `null`.

**Side effects** — writes an audit trail entry (`adminDetails/save`) into the audit collection before the write is attempted, so the attempt is recorded even if the save subsequently fails.

requestBody.description: Full administrator document. `companyId` identifies the tenant and is effectively mandatory — every read path filters on it. Omit `id` to insert; supply it to replace an existing document wholesale.

500.description: Either the service returned an empty entity (`status: FAILURE`, no `error` key), or the MongoDB write threw — a malformed `id` that is not a valid `ObjectId`, a duplicate key, or the cluster being unreachable. When an exception was caught its message is echoed in `error`.

200.description: Administrator persisted. `value` holds the saved `AdminDetailsEntity` including the generated or reused `id`.

400.description: Malformed JSON body, or a type mismatch on a field. Rejected by Spring's message converter before the controller runs, so the response is Spring's default error body rather than the standard envelope.

get.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — populates the "type of organisation" dropdown on the company registration form (`userDetails/registration` stores the chosen value in `type_of_organization`).

**Database behaviour** — **no MongoDB access.** The list is read from the `organization.types` application property and split on commas at request time. Changing the list therefore requires a configuration change and a restart, not a data update.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`workplaceHierarchy/getOrganization`).

500.description: The `organization.types` property is missing or unresolvable, so splitting it threw.

200.description: `value` is an array of organisation-type strings.

get.summary: List all users in a company
get.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — renders the user-management grid for a tenant.

**Database behaviour** — a derived-query `find({ "company_id": <companyId> })` over `table_admin_user_details`. No paging or sort.

**Type note** — the path variable arrives as a `String` but `company_id` is stored as an **`int`**. Pass a plain numeric string (`1001`); a non-numeric value will not match anything and yields an empty array rather than an error.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`userDetails/getAllUser`).

parameters.name: companyId
parameters.description: Numeric business tenant identifier, passed as a path segment. Not a Mongo `ObjectId`.

200.description: `value` is the array of directory users; `[]` when the company has none or the id is unknown.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

get.summary: List every project in the catalogue
get.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — populates project pickers, most visibly the multi-select on the public demo-request form.

**Database behaviour** — an unfiltered `find({})` over `table_admin_project_details`. No paging or sorting; the catalogue is small and intended to be fetched whole.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`project/fetchAllProject`).

500.description: The MongoDB read threw — typically a connection or timeout failure.

200.description: `value` is the array of project documents; `[]` when the catalogue has not been seeded.

get.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — shows the tenant's subscription history and current entitlements on the billing / products screen.

**Database behaviour** — a derived-query `find({ "company_id": <companyId> })` over `table_product_purchase`. No date filter is applied, so **expired subscriptions are returned alongside active ones** — compare `endDate` against the current date client-side if you need only live entitlements.

**Parameter style** — `companyId` is an unannotated method argument, which Spring binds as an **optional query parameter** (`?companyId=1001`). Omitting it does not fail the request: `companyId` arrives as `null`, the query matches documents whose `company_id` is null, and you get an empty array with `status: SUCCESS`.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`productPurchase/getPurchaseProductByCompanyId`).

**Cosmetic quirk** — the response's `urlPath` is hardcoded to `countryList`, a copy-paste artefact. Ignore it.

parameters.name: companyId
parameters.description: Business tenant identifier, passed as a query parameter — for example `?companyId=1001`. Not a Mongo `ObjectId`. Technically optional; omitting it yields an empty result rather than an error.

200.description: `value` is the array of subscription documents; `[]` when the company has none, the id is unknown, or the parameter was omitted.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

get.summary: List the catalogue with a company's subscription state
get.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — renders the tenant's product page: every available product, each flagged with whether this company has already bought it.

**Database behaviour** — a two-collection read. The service first fetches all documents from `table_product_master`, then resolves the company's subscriptions from `table_product_purchase` and decorates each product with the `@Transient` `isPurchased` flag and, where applicable, the matching `productPurchase` sub-object. The join is performed in Java, not via a `$lookup` aggregation.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`productMaster/productList/{companyId}`).

**Cosmetic quirk** — the response's `urlPath` is hardcoded to `countryList`, a copy-paste artefact. It carries no meaning here; ignore it.

parameters.name: companyId
parameters.description: Business tenant identifier whose subscription state should decorate the catalogue. This is the company number used throughout the module, **not** a 24-character Mongo `ObjectId`.

500.description: Either MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

200.description: `value` is the array of products, each carrying `isPurchased` and — when subscribed — a nested `productPurchase`. An unknown `companyId` still returns the full catalogue, with every product marked `isPurchased: false`.

get.summary: Fetch the authenticated company's holiday calendar
get.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — renders the holiday calendar for the signed-in user's company.

**Company scope comes from the token, not the request.** The controller reads the `companyID` request attribute that the JWT authentication filter sets after decoding the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. There is no path variable, query parameter or body — you cannot request another company's calendar through this route, and a call without a valid token resolves `companyID` to `null` and yields an empty calendar.

**Database behaviour** — a derived-query `find({ "company_id": <companyID> })` over `table_holiday`. No date-range filter is applied, so past and future holidays are returned together; filter client-side by `date` or `repeatType`.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`holiday/getHoliday`).

**Unusual status code** — an empty calendar returns `204 NO CONTENT` **with a JSON body** carrying `status: FAILURE` and `statusCode: 204`. Most HTTP clients treat `204` as bodyless and will discard that payload, so branch on the status code rather than trying to parse the envelope.

200.description: `value` is the array of holiday documents for the authenticated company.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw. `error` carries the driver message.

204.description: No holidays configured for the company — also what an unauthenticated call produces, since `companyID` resolves to `null`. A body is written but most clients will not surface it.

get.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — backs the internal sales dashboard that works the demo queue.

**Database behaviour** — an unfiltered `find({})` over `table_admin_demo_request`. There is no filter on `demo_status`, no paging and no sort, so completed and pending leads come back together and the payload grows without bound as leads accumulate.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`demo/fetchDemoRequest`).

**Exposure note** — the response contains prospect names, e-mail addresses and mobile numbers. Restrict this route to internal callers.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw — typically a connection or timeout failure.

200.description: `value` is the array of demo request documents; `[]` when the queue is empty.

get.summary: Resolve the primary locality for a postal code within a country
get.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — the single-result variant of `getAddressUsingPincode`, for forms that want one address pre-filled rather than a list to choose from.

**Database behaviour** — **no MongoDB access.** Calls the same external KPOST address service and returns only the **first** entry of the upstream result list.

**Caveat** — because the implementation indexes element `0` unconditionally, a pincode with no upstream matches raises an `IndexOutOfBoundsException` and the endpoint answers `500`, not an empty `200`. Callers that must tolerate unknown pincodes should prefer `getAddressUsingPincode/{pincode}`.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`country/getAddressUsingPincodeAndCountry`).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country the pincode belongs to. Accepted as a path segment for future multi-country routing; the current implementation resolves the address from the pincode alone and does not filter on this value.

200.description: `value` is a single untyped address map — the first locality matching the pincode.

500.description: No locality matched the pincode (see the caveat above), or the upstream address service failed. `error` carries the exception message.

get.summary: Resolve all localities for a postal code
get.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — auto-fills address forms. Given a pincode the caller gets back every matching locality so the user can pick their area instead of typing state, city and district by hand. Used by employee residential/mailing address capture and by workplace location set-up.

**Database behaviour** — **no MongoDB access.** The service issues an outbound HTTP call to the external KPOST address service and maps its JSON response into a list of loose key/value maps. Response shape is therefore dictated by that upstream service, not by a local schema, and network latency dominates the call.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`country/getAddressUsingPincode`).

parameters.name: pincode
parameters.description: Postal / PIN code to resolve. Passed straight through to the upstream service with no validation, so a non-numeric value simply returns no matches.

200.description: `value` is an array of untyped locality maps (keys such as `Name`, `State`, `District`, `Country`, as returned upstream). An unknown pincode yields an empty array with `status: SUCCESS` — **not** a `404`.

500.description: The upstream address service was unreachable, timed out, or returned a payload that could not be parsed. `error` carries the underlying exception message.

get.summary: List every country in the catalogue
get.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — populates country and dial-code dropdowns across the admin UI (company registration, employee residential/mailing address, workplace locations).

**Database behaviour** — an unfiltered `find({})` over the `table_admin_country` collection returning every document. There is no paging, sorting or projection, so the whole catalogue crosses the wire on each call; cache it client-side.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`country/countryList`).

200.description: `value` is the array of country documents. An empty catalogue yields `[]` with `status: SUCCESS` — it is not treated as an error.

500.description: The MongoDB read threw — typically a connection or timeout failure. `error` carries the driver message.

get.summary: List every workplace node across all companies
get.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — a platform-level diagnostic / export read. It is **not** tenant-scoped.

**Database behaviour** — an unfiltered `find({})` over `table_admin_tier_variable`, returning every node belonging to every company with no paging, sort or projection.

**Use with care** — because there is no `company_id` filter, the response mixes tenants together and grows linearly with the whole platform's hierarchy data. For anything user-facing prefer `getAdminTierVariable`, which is scoped by company and parent.

**Side effects** — read-only apart from the audit entry (`adminTierVariable/getAllVariable`).

500.description: The MongoDB read threw — on a large collection most often a cursor timeout.

200.description: `value` is every node document in the collection.
OK

delete.description:
**Why use this endpoint** — removes a user from the company directory, revoking their hierarchy scope.

**Database behaviour** — `deleteUser(id)` against `table_admin_user_details`. A hard delete with no soft-delete flag and no recovery path. This is the only endpoint in the module that uses the `DELETE` HTTP verb with a path variable.

**Scope caveat** — deleting the directory entry does **not** remove the matching credentials from `table_admin_user_signup`, so the person may still be able to authenticate. Remove or disable the sign-up record separately.

**Side effects** — destructive. Audited as `userDetails/delete`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The 24-character hex `ObjectId` of the `table_admin_user_details` document to delete. Note this is the Mongo document id, **not** the `userID` login name.

200.description: User deleted. `value` is the literal string `SUCCESS`.

500.description: The service reported anything other than `SUCCESS` — commonly no matching document — or the delete threw.

id.description: MongoDB `_id` as a 24-character hex `ObjectId` string. Omit to insert; supply to target an existing document.

attributeId.description: The level of the position being wired. Stored as `attribute_id`.

variableId.description: The node being wired. Stored as `variable_id`.

parentAttributeId.description: Level of the structural parent. Stored as `parent_attribute_id`.

parentVariableId.description: The structural parent node. Stored as `parent_variable_id`. Null at the top of the tree.

reportingAttributeId.description: Level of the node this position reports to. Stored as `reporting_attribute_id`.

reportingVariableId.description: The node this position reports to. Stored as `reporting_variable_id`. Independent of `parentVariableId`.

reportingParentAttributeId.description: Level of the reporting target's own parent. Stored as `reporting_parent_attribute_id`.

reportingParentVariableId.description: The reporting target's own parent node. Stored as `reporting_parent_variable_id`.

workplaceJson.description: Denormalised **JSON string** (not a nested object — escape it accordingly) capturing the resolved workplace path at write time. Copied onto role postings and **never refreshed** when the hierarchy later changes.

reportingJson.description: Denormalised **JSON string** capturing the resolved reporting path at write time. Same snapshot semantics as `workplaceJson`.

abbreviation.description: Short form for this hierarchy link.

code.description: Generated code for this hierarchy link.

WorkPlaceHierarchy.description:
An **edge** of the workplace graph, stored in the `table_admin_workplace_hierarchy` MongoDB collection. Where `AdminTierVariable` holds the nodes, this document holds the wiring between them.

Four attribute/variable id pairs are recorded — the position itself, its structural parent, its reporting counterpart, and that counterpart's parent — plus two denormalised JSON-string snapshots of the resolved paths. Null fields are omitted from responses.

value.description: The operation payload. Depending on the endpoint this is a single document, an array of documents, a plain status string such as `SUCCESS`, or a map of generated values. Absent when the operation failed before producing a payload.

statusCode.description: Application-level status code, mirroring the HTTP status. `200` on success, `500` on any handled failure (including "document not found" conditions). `204` is used by `holiday/getHoliday` when the company has no holidays configured.

urlPath.description: Echo of the endpoint path fragment that produced this response — useful for client-side log correlation.

error.description: Exception message captured by the controller's catch block. Present only when `status` is `FAILURE` and an exception was thrown (a MongoDB timeout, a duplicate-key violation, a null `_id`, a malformed `ObjectId`, and so on).

message.description: Human-readable note. Emitted by a subset of endpoints — for example `holiday/saveHoliday` ("Holiday already exists"), `userDetails/sendOTP` and `userDetails/validateOTP`.

ApiResponseEnvelope.description: Standard response envelope returned by every Admin Module endpoint. The concrete type of `value` varies per operation and is described in that operation's `description`.

id.description: MongoDB `_id` as a 24-character hex `ObjectId` string. Omit on create; supply to target an existing document.

attributeId.description: The level this value belongs to — the `_id` of an `Attribute`. Stored as `attribute_id`.

companyId.description: Owning tenant, stored as `company_id`. The business company number, not an `ObjectId`.

variableName.description: Display name of the value. Stored as `variable_name`.

parentVariableId.description: Structural parent node. Stored as `parent_variable_id`. **Null for a root value**; children are resolved by querying this field.

parentAttributeId.description: The level the structural parent sits at. Stored as `parent_attribute_id`. Null for a root value.

abbreviation.description: Short form derived from `variableName` by the service on save.

code.description: Generated value code, unique within the company.

Variable.description:
A **node** of the base hierarchy — a value sitting at a level defined by `Attribute`. Maps to the `table_admin_variable` MongoDB collection.

Carries **no `reporting_*` fields**: this pair models structure only. Null fields are omitted from responses.

id.description: MongoDB `_id` as a 24-character hex `ObjectId` string. Assigned on insert.

dialCode.description: International dial code as an **integer** (no leading `+`). Stored as `dial_code`. Sending a quoted string produces a `400`.

mobileNumber.description: Destination mobile number, national format without the dial code. Stored as `mobile_number`.

otp.description: The one-time code. Generated by `sendOTP` and **never returned** in its response; the client supplies it back on `validateOTP`. Valid for 10 minutes. No attempt counter or lockout is implemented, so this value is brute-forceable within that window.

type.description: Purpose of the OTP — mirrors the `requestType` used when it was sent, and selects the SMS template (see `KpostSMSTemplate`).

sendDate.description: When the OTP was issued. Stored as `send_date` and defaulted to now on insert.

expireDate.description: When the OTP lapses — 10 minutes after issue. Stored as `expire_date` and checked by `validateOTP`.

otpValidationStatus.description: Consumption flag stored as `otp_validation_status`: `'N'` until the code is successfully validated, then `'Y'`. A single character, not a boolean.

otpExpireStatus.description: Expiry flag stored as `otp_expire_status`: `'N'` while live, `'Y'` once expired. A single character, not a boolean.

createdBy.description: Origin of the request. Stored as `created_by` and defaulted to `USER`.

userID.description: **`@Transient` — never persisted.** Optional login name carried alongside the verification for flow context.

OtpValidation.description:
An issued one-time password, stored in the `table_admin_otp_validation` MongoDB collection.

A document is inserted by `sendOTP` and consumed by `validateOTP`, which flips `otpValidationStatus` to `'Y'` so the code cannot be replayed. As a **request** body only `mobileNumber`, `otp`, `dialCode` and `type` are read; every other field is managed server-side.

This entity has **no `@JsonInclude(NON_NULL)`**, so null fields are serialised in responses.

id.description: MongoDB `_id` as a 24-character hex `ObjectId` string. This is what `DELETE userDetails/delete/{id}` expects — not the `userID` login name.

companyId.description: Owning tenant, stored as `company_id`. **An `int` here**, unlike the `String` `companyId` used by almost every other collection in the module — sending a quoted string produces a `400`.

userID.description: Login name, correlating this directory entry with the credentials in `table_admin_user_signup`. Stored as `user_id`.

variableIds.description: Hierarchy nodes this user is scoped to, as an embedded array of **free-form maps** — the inner shape is not schema-enforced and varies by caller (typically `attributeId` / `variableId` pairs). Note the Mongo field keeps its camelCase name, `variableIds`. **Replaced wholesale on update**, so send the complete list or you will silently revoke access.

additionalProperties.description: Hierarchy nodes this user is scoped to, as an embedded array of **free-form maps** — the inner shape is not schema-enforced and varies by caller (typically `attributeId` / `variableId` pairs). Note the Mongo field keeps its camelCase name, `variableIds`. **Replaced wholesale on update**, so send the complete list or you will silently revoke access.

items.description: Hierarchy nodes this user is scoped to, as an embedded array of **free-form maps** — the inner shape is not schema-enforced and varies by caller (typically `attributeId` / `variableId` pairs). Note the Mongo field keeps its camelCase name, `variableIds`. **Replaced wholesale on update**, so send the complete list or you will silently revoke access.

reportingVariableIds.description: Reporting-branch nodes this user is scoped to, same free-form map shape as `variableIds`. Stored as `reporting_variable_ids` and likewise replaced wholesale on update.

additionalProperties.description: Reporting-branch nodes this user is scoped to, same free-form map shape as `variableIds`. Stored as `reporting_variable_ids` and likewise replaced wholesale on update.

items.description: Reporting-branch nodes this user is scoped to, same free-form map shape as `variableIds`. Stored as `reporting_variable_ids` and likewise replaced wholesale on update.

gender.description: Gender as free text; no enumeration is enforced.

mobileNumber.description: Contact mobile number, national format without a dial code. Stored as `mobile_number`.

UserDetails.description:
A user in a company's directory, stored in the `table_admin_user_details` MongoDB collection. The `variableIds` arrays scope what the user can see in the admin UI.

This is **not** the login record — credentials live separately in `table_admin_user_signup` (`UserSignUp`). Deleting a directory user does not remove their ability to authenticate. Null fields are omitted from responses.

id.description: MongoDB `_id` as a 24-character hex `ObjectId` string. Assigned on sign-up.

userName.description: The person's display name. Stored as `user_name`. Also the raw material for `generateUserIdSuggestions`.

mobileNumber.description: Mobile number, national format without a dial code. Stored as `mobile_number`. Verified through `sendOTP` / `validateOTP`.

emailID.description: E-mail address. Stored as `email_id`. Not format-validated server-side.

userID.description: Login name. Stored as `user_id` and must be unique — but `checkAvailability` does **not** reserve it, so two concurrent sign-ups can both pass the check.

password.description: Account password. **Stored in clear text** — the application configures a `NoOpPasswordEncoder`, so no hashing is applied. Never log this value, and never echo it back to a client.

createdDate.description: When the account was created. Stored as `created_date` and **defaulted to now** — omit it on sign-up.

RolePosting.description:
A **seat in the organisation**: a position defined by a workplace node, an HR node and a physical location, which an employee may or may not currently occupy. Stored in the `table_admin_role_posting` MongoDB collection.

Key modelling points:

* **A null `employeeId` is a vacancy.** Creating the seat and filling it are separate steps.
* **The `*Json` fields are denormalised JSON strings, not nested objects** — snapshots of the resolved hierarchy path taken when the posting was written. They are deliberately not refreshed when the hierarchy later changes, so a posting records where the person sat *then*.
* **Lifecycle runs through `activeStatus`**, not deletion. Suspension and termination flip the boolean and record `reason`, `remarks`, `duration` and `rejoiningDate`.
* **Every `@Transient` field below is computed on read and never stored.**

Null fields are omitted from responses.

workplaceLocationId.description: Physical sites for the seats being created — a **list** on this request object even though a stored posting holds a single `workplaceLocationId`. Used by `rolePosting/save`.

items.description: Physical sites for the seats being created — a **list** on this request object even though a stored posting holds a single `workplaceLocationId`. Used by `rolePosting/save`.

rolePostingId.description: The seat being filled — the `_id` of a `RolePosting` document. Stored as `role_posting_id`. Not validated to exist.

contactEmailId.description: Contact e-mail address. Stored as `contact_email_id`. Not format-validated server-side.

AdminTierVariable.description:
A **node** of the workplace hierarchy — *South Region*, *Chennai Zone* — attached to a level defined by `AdminTierAttribute`. Maps to the `table_admin_tier_variable` MongoDB collection.

The tree is modelled with **self-referencing id strings, not embedded sub-documents**, and two independent link sets are stored side by side:

* `parentVariableId` / `parentAttributeId` — structural containment.
* `reportingVariableId` / `reportingAttributeId` / `reportingJson` — the reporting line, which may deliberately differ from the structural parent.

Null fields are omitted from responses.
